summary: The data side is broad and mostly matches Terraria's stats: 660 item GLBs and 1,554 icon files, correct use/speed/knockback tables, prefixes, a reforge service, ammo classes and minions. The presentation layer is where it stops feeling like Terraria. Every item goes through 8 generic upper-body clips chosen by `ActionFor`. So boss summons, crystals, mirrors, crates and food all play "drink", and boomerangs, shuriken, bombs, yoyos and flails all play the two-handed gun-recoil pose. The data field `useStyle: "hold"` is never used. Melee is inconsistent: the hitbox and trail sweep horizontally and linearly from the first tick, while the arm plays an overhead arc with a wind-up. Tools restart their animation mid-swing whenever useTime is shorter than useAnimation. Yoyos, flails and whips are plain returning projectiles or melee arcs, with no string, chain, lash or minion tag. The `trail` colour set on projectiles in the data is never drawn, and all shots spawn from the eye. Around the items: rarity 9 and 10 (52 items) show as yellow; dropped items are flat, non-spinning icon billboards; pickups show as corner toasts rather than Terraria's "Copper Ore (5)" popup; coins never convert up and there are no coin or ammo slots; prefixes use invented names and don't show in tooltips; icons are soft 3D renders with no outline, and gun icons are rendered from underneath. Worn armor is not drawn on the character at all.

findings.title: Use-style vocabulary is too coarse; many item families play the wrong body action
findings.evidence: enum UseStyle { None, Swing, Thrust, Shoot, Hold, Consume, Place }. useStyle counts in data: swing 151, shoot 129, consume 54, thrust 22, place 1, hold 0. ActionFor checks in order: Consume/UseStyle.Consume -> "drink"; IsTool -> "mine"; Thrust; Melee -> "swing"; Magic/Summon/ManaCost -> "cast"; Shoot -> UseAmmo=="arrow" ? "bow" : "shoot"; else "use". Results: slime_crown and suspicious_looking_eye (useStyle consume) drink; life_crystal and mana_crystal drink; magic_mirror, cooked_fish and wooden_crate drink; wooden_boomerang, shuriken, throwing_knife, bomb, grenade, wood_yoyo and ball_o_hurt get the two-handed gun kick ('shoot'); laser_rifle (a magic gun) gets the palm-push 'cast'. ItemDef.SoundSet and AnimationSet are never read anywhere.
findings.terraria_reference: ItemUseStyleID: 1 Swing (swords, tools, boomerangs, thrown items, blocks), 2 EatFood, 4 HoldUp (life/mana crystals, boss summons), 5 Shoot (guns, bows, staffs, flails, yoyos), 6 mirror/hold style, 9 DrinkLiquid (potions), 13 Rapier (1.4 shortswords), 14 RaiseLamp (torches), plus whip-specific animation. Each item declares its style explicitly.
findings.fix: Replace the enum with Terraria-aligned styles: Swing, Rapier, Spear, Shoot(Gun), Bow, Staff, Tome, HoldUp, Drink, Eat, Throw, Flail, Yoyo, Whip, Place, Lamp. Make PlayerAvatar.ActionFor switch on item.UseStyle first and only infer when it is None. Author new clips in tools/blender/bgen/human/actions.py: hold_up (item raised overhead), eat, throw (overhand release at ~0.35), flail_spin, yoyo_hold, whip_crack and place (a short swing). Add them to HumanoidAnimator.Actions. Migrate the data: boss summons and crystals to holdUp, food to eat, crates to holdUp, thrown weapons and boomerangs to throw, flails to flail, yoyos to yoyo, whips to whip, magic guns to shoot. Either wire ItemDef.AnimationSet/SoundSet as per-item overrides or delete them. Add a ContentValidator rule that every weapon or consumable declares a style.

findings.title: Melee swing: hitbox, trail and arm animation disagree in plane, timing and size
findings.evidence: MeleeSystem: 'the blade sweeps a horizontal arc'; current = halfArc - t*2*halfArc with t = Tick/Duration, linear from tick 1. SwingTrail draws the same flat arc starting at Age 0. The third-person 'swing' clip is 'Terraria's overhead arc': pitch 178->208 wind-up over t 0-0.22, strike at 0.46. So the hitbox and trail finish half the arc before the blade has left the wind-up. First person sweeps diagonally from over the right shoulder (rotation X 0.9->-1.6). Reach: breaker_blade has meleeSwing length 5.2 cells = 2.6 m + 0.6 m, but its model blade is 1.3 m (assets.json length 1.3). Prefix Size scales the hitbox (MeleeSystem.cs:99) but not the trail (SwingTrail.cs:62) or the held model (HeldScale ignores the stack). MeleeSwingParams.TrailColor is never read, and no data sets it.
findings.terraria_reference: The sword sprite rotates from behind and above the head, down in front of the player, over useAnimation. The hitbox is the sprite's rectangle each frame, so what you see is what hits. Item.scale and size prefixes (Large, Massive, Legendary) visibly enlarge the blade.
findings.fix: Add a shared swing curve in Core, e.g. `Strata.Core.Gameplay.Entities.SwingCurve.Angle(t)`, using the same keyframes as actions.py (wind-up 0-0.2, strike 0.2-0.5, follow-through). Sweep in the vertical plane containing the aim and world-up, from about +110 degrees above the aim to about -70 degrees below. Use it in MeleeSystem.Connects, SwingTrail.DrawArc and ViewModel. Better still, have SwingTrail sample the held node's blade tip each frame (PlayerAvatar exposes it) and build the ribbon from real positions. Scale the held model by Prefixes.Size(stack), and derive the hit length from the model length (or vice versa) via a `reach` param in assets.json. Colour the trail with Swing.TrailColor ?? rarity colour.

findings.title: Tools (pickaxes/axes/hammers): animation restarts mid-swing; speed bonuses shorten useTime only
findings.evidence: p.UseCooldown = useTime and p.UseAnimation = item.UseAnimation, and a new use is allowed when the cooldown ends. Copper Pickaxe has useTime 15 / useAnimation 21, so the 21-tick 'mine' clip is re-fired at 71%. Lunar pickaxes (6/12) and the Spectre Hamaxe (7/14) re-fire at 50%. The avatar restarts the action whenever `use > _lastUse`. The mining speed bonus (line 110), melee speed (line 158) and prefix UseSpeed (line 97) divide only useTime. MeleeSystem Duration, SwingTrail Duration and ViewModel t all use the unscaled item.UseAnimation. With Feral Claws (+12%) swords restart their swing before it finishes.
findings.terraria_reference: One use lasts useAnimation. Within it, a tool acts every useTime (e.g. a pickaxe hits the tile about 1.4 times per swing), and the swing visual always completes. Melee speed scales both useAnimation and useTime.
findings.fix: Split PlayerEntity into ItemAnimation (visual/swing window, with an effective max stored on the entity) and ItemTime (action cadence). Start a new animation only when ItemAnimation reaches 0 and the button is still held. Inside the window, run tool hits every scaled useTime. Apply melee, mining and prefix speed to both values, and have PlayerAvatar, ViewModel, SwingTrail and MeleeSystem read the entity's effective animation length rather than item.UseAnimation.

findings.title: Held-item grip/orientation is generic (+90 deg about X); no muzzle/tip sockets; first-person guns point skyward
findings.evidence: Third person: node.RotationDegrees = (90,0,0); Position = (0,0.08,0) for every item on hand.R. HeldScale is 1 for weapons, 0.95 for lights and 0.3 for furniture. First person: Rest (0.32,-0.3,-0.55), rotation (-0.35,0.25,0.15), so the item's +Y points about 70 degrees upward. Shoot, cast, bow and use only add a 0.08 m lift (lines 69-72), so first-person guns and bows fire with the barrel at the sky and no recoil. There are no grip, muzzle or tip empties in the Blender pipeline (grep finds none). Every projectile spawns at p.Eye + dir*0.4, not at the weapon.
findings.terraria_reference: Guns and bows are held out along the cursor direction with per-item holdoutOffset. Staffs (Item.staff[] set) are held angled with the gem toward the cursor. Bows are held vertically. Projectiles leave the barrel or bow and muzzle position is per item. Swords rotate with the swing.
findings.fix: Add hold data per generator in tools/blender/assets.json, e.g. params.grip {offset, euler, scale} and params.muzzle. Export them as named empties ('grip', 'muzzle') in the GLB (bgen/export.py), with defaults per generator: bow limbs vertical, gun barrel along the aim, staff tilted 30 degrees, sword edge in the swing plane. PlayerAvatar.UpdateHeld and ViewModel.UpdateItem should read the empties (fall back to today's 90 degrees). ViewModel needs per-action rest poses: gun/bow/staff/tome aimed at the crosshair with a recoil kick on Shot, drink raised to the camera, hold-up above the view. Add an optional origin to ShotRequest, computed in Core from Eye + aim-relative muzzle offset, and use it in ProjectileSystem.Fire.

findings.title: Bows: string-draw clip is out of sync with the arrow; every metal bow is identical
findings.evidence: The bow clip draws from t 0 to 0.5 and releases at 0.6-0.66, but ItemUseSystem.Shoot spawns the arrow on the first tick of the use, so the arrow leaves while the string is still being pulled. All 17 '{metal}_bow' items use one generator with limbLayer 'iron', so they differ only by tint. The Daedalus Stormbow ('Shoots arrows from the sky') fires 3 arrows from the eye with spread 14.
findings.terraria_reference: The bow is held out toward the cursor, the arrow leaves at once with no draw pause, and the bow sprite differs per tier. The Daedalus Stormbow rains arrows from above the cursor.
findings.fix: Re-key the bow clip so it releases at t≈0.05 and re-draws over the rest of the use (the visual then matches the instant shot). Give the bow generator per-tier params (limb curvature, tip ornaments, grip wrap colour) in assets.json patterns keyed by metal. Add ShootProjectileParams.From = 'sky' (spawn above the aim point) for the Stormbow and the Starfury.

findings.title: Guns: no muzzle flash, burst fired all at once, unreadable icons, magic guns use the cast pose
findings.evidence: The third-person 'shoot' clip has a recoil kick (good). CombatEffects only does damage numbers, explosions and puffs: there is no muzzle flash, light or smoke on Shot. clockwork_assault_rifle ('Three round burst') is count 3, spread 2, so the three bullets spawn on the same tick. The Laser Rifle (damageType magic) plays 'cast' because the Magic check precedes the Shoot check. Bullets are a 0.45 m emissive capsule (fine).
findings.terraria_reference: A small muzzle flash and sound per shot; the Clockwork Assault Rifle fires 3 sequential shots per use; magic guns (Laser Rifle, Space Gun) are held like guns; the sprite has recoil.
findings.fix: Subscribe to ItemUse.Shot in CombatEffects to spawn a 0.05 s OmniLight plus an additive flash quad at the muzzle socket (see the grip finding), coloured by ammo. Add ShootProjectileParams.Burst {count, intervalTicks} and queue the shots in ItemUseSystem/PlayerEntity. Route magic guns to the gun style via the explicit useStyle (see the use-style finding).

findings.title: Projectile trails defined in data but never rendered; magic bolts are tiny spheres
findings.evidence: ProjectileDef.Trail (e.g. "trail": "#ffb060" on flaming_arrow, spark, every gem bolt, the enchanted beam and the starfury star) has zero readers in C# (grep '.Trail' finds nothing). Bolts are rendered as SphereMesh radius = Def.Radius*0.25 (0.35 -> 0.0875 m) with an emissive material and one OmniLight. The 'spark' visual has no special case. The Starfury ('Causes stars to rain from the sky') shoots its star from the eye.
findings.terraria_reference: Gem staff bolts, Flamelash, Water Bolt and Starfury stars all leave coloured dust trails; the stars fall from the sky toward the cursor.
findings.fix: In ProjectileRenderer.Create, when Def.Trail != null, add a GPUParticles3D or ImmediateMesh ribbon with Def.Trail as the colour ramp start (fade to alpha 0 over about 0.25 s). Scale bolt cores to at least 0.12 m and add a billboarded additive halo. Add ShootProjectileParams.From ('eye'/'muzzle'/'sky') and use 'sky' for the Starfury.

findings.title: Thrown weapons (shuriken, knives, bombs, grenades) use the gun pose and don't spin
findings.evidence: Shuriken, throwing_knife (ranged) and bomb, dynamite, grenade (useStyle shoot) fall through to action 'shoot' (two hands on a barrel with a recoil kick). ProjectileRenderer tumbles only `Returns > 0 || Fuse`, so a shuriken (no returns, no fuse) flies without spinning.
findings.terraria_reference: Thrown items use style 1 (overhand arm swing and release); shuriken spin rapidly and bombs tumble.
findings.fix: Add a 'throw' clip (overhand, release at about 35%) and useStyle 'throw' in the data. Add ProjectileDef.Spin (rad/s, default 0; shuriken 30, knives 0, bombs 6) and use it in ProjectileRenderer in place of the Returns/Fuse heuristic.

findings.title: Yoyos are fire-and-return boomerangs with no string or cursor control
findings.evidence: wood_yoyo projectile: returns 40, pierce -1, lifetime 120, so it flies straight for 40 ticks then homes back to the owner. Lines are drawn only for bobbers (`if (p.Def.Bobber)`), so there is no string. The flying yoyo mesh includes the modelled string stub (gear.py:194-195). The master plan lists 'Whips/yoyos/summons' as not done.
findings.terraria_reference: While the button is held the yoyo stays out on a visible string, hovering toward the cursor within its range (Wooden Yoyo about 9.5 tiles) with a per-item lifetime; releasing reels it in. It spins constantly and grinds enemies.
findings.fix: Add ProjectileDef.Tether {kind: 'yoyo'|'flail', range, lifetimeTicks}. In ProjectileSystem.Special add TickYoyo: while the owner holds use_primary (pass the held state via PlayerEntity), steer toward Eye + Aim * min(range, target distance) with capped speed, clear HitNpcs every 10 ticks, and return on release or timeout. In ProjectileRenderer draw a line from the hand socket to the projectile for any Tether def (reuse the bobber _lines path), and spin the model about its axle. Export a separate head-only GLB (e.g. wood_yoyo_head) and set the projectile model to it.

findings.title: Flails fly as the whole flail model (handle included) with no chain
findings.evidence: The ball_o_hurt, sunfury, blue_moon and flower_pow projectiles use visual 'item' with returns 26-28 and pierce -1. The renderer loads the item model, which is handle + chain + ball, and tumbles the whole thing at 22 rad/s. No chain is drawn back to the hand. The avatar plays the gun 'shoot' clip.
findings.terraria_reference: The flail spins around the player while the button is held, launches toward the cursor on release, drags along the ground and retracts, with a chain drawn from the hand to the ball the whole time.
findings.fix: Use the Tether mechanism from the yoyo finding with kind 'flail': an orbit phase while held (radius 1.2 m around the hand), launch at ShootSpeed on release, then retract. Render chain links with a GrappleVisual-style link strip from the hand socket. Export the ball as its own GLB (flail generator option head_only) for the projectile model. Add a 'flail_spin' clip (arm circling overhead).

findings.title: Whips are just wide melee arcs: no lash, no tip, no minion tag
findings.evidence: leather_whip is meleeSwing arc 110, length 5.5 cells; snapthorn is arc 110, length 6.5. Their descriptions promise 'Your summons will focus struck enemies' and 'Inflicts poison', but grep finds no whip, tag or focus code in src. The held model is a static coil (gear.py:176) and the icon renders it as an unreadable zigzag. As melee items, whips auto-repeat.
findings.terraria_reference: The whip is a segmented lash that extends over the swing and cracks at the tip. It hits every enemy along its path with damage falling off per hit, applies a tag debuff that boosts minion damage and makes minions target the struck enemy, and has a crit-tip sound and particles.
findings.fix: Add ItemBehaviorSpecs 'whip' {length, segments, tagDamage, tagBuff} and a Core WhipSystem: a lash polyline on a bezier driven by t over useAnimation, testing hits along the segments, and on hit applying the tag buff (a BuffDef with a minionTag effect) that ProjectileSystem.TickMinion reads to pick its target and add flat damage. Render the lash in the game layer as a tapered ImmediateMesh tube (like SwingTrail) with the handle model in hand. Add a 'whip_crack' clip. Re-render the icon with the lash laid out as an S-curve.

findings.title: Boomerangs: flight and return work, but the throw pose is wrong
findings.evidence: returns 28-36, one out at a time (line 335), and they tumble at 22 rad/s (good). The pose is the gun 'shoot' clip because the damageType is melee but there is no meleeSwing behavior. The spin is about local X after aligning +Y to the velocity, i.e. end-over-end rather than a flat whirl.
findings.terraria_reference: Boomerangs use style 1 (an overhand throw) and spin flat in the plane of flight.
findings.fix: Use the 'throw' style and clip. For returning projectiles, spin about the model's plane normal (after aligning, rotate about the local Y/normal axis rather than Right).

findings.title: Spears and shortswords: thrust exists but the model never extends to the hitbox
findings.evidence: Thrust length is 3.2-4.2 cells, i.e. 1.6-2.1 m + 0.4 m from the chest. The spear model is 1.1 m (gear.py:215) and stays in the hand, moved only by the arm lunge. The thrust trail is a single quad 0.14 m wide (side*0.07). ThrustTolerance is 0.7 m.
findings.terraria_reference: Spears are held projectiles: the shaft slides out past the hand along the aim to its full reach, then retracts. 1.4 shortswords (Rapier style 13) are a quick stab in any direction with a visible thrust sprite.
findings.fix: In PlayerAvatar and ViewModel, translate the held node along its axis by (thrustLength - modelLength) * sin(pi*t), in sync with the melee progress, so the tip reaches the hit capsule end. Widen the thrust streak and add a tip sparkle at the end.

findings.title: Summon staves: minions render well, but the pose, spawn point and minion indicator are missing
findings.evidence: Minions use creature GLBs (gel, vulture, imp) with a tint and face their flight (good). Staves play 'cast'. Minions spawn at the eye with shootSpeed 3. Nothing in game/UI mentions minions (grep 'minion' finds only ProjectileRenderer), so there is no minion buff or slot count, and oldest minions are silently replaced (MakeRoomForMinion).
findings.terraria_reference: The staff is raised (use style 1) and the minion appears at the cursor with a dust burst. A buff icon (e.g. 'Baby Slime') shows the minion is active and can be right-clicked to dismiss it; minion count and slot usage are visible.
findings.fix: Spawn minions at the aim point (clamped to reach) with a one-shot particle puff in ProjectileRenderer.Create for Minion defs. Add a synthetic buff per active minion type in the HUD buff row (Hud.cs buff list) with count and right-click to dismiss (ProjectileSystem.MinionsOf). Give summon staves the hold_up/swing style.

findings.title: Hooks: one generic chain and claw for every hook; item models unused
findings.evidence: A metal diamond-link chain and a procedural 3-prong claw tinted by GrappleParams.Color. Nine hook item GLBs exist (assets.json generator 'hook') but none is used for the head. Gem hooks differ only in tint, and the Ivy Whip draws a metal chain. The grappling_hook description leaks a keybind: 'Get over here! (press F to throw)'.
findings.terraria_reference: Each hook has its own head and chain sprite: gem hooks show the gem head and gem chain, the Ivy Whip a vine. Hooks go in a dedicated equip slot.
findings.fix: Add to GrappleParams: head (item model id, default the hook item) and chain ('links'|'vine'|'gem'). Render the head with PropLibrary.Model(AssetPaths.ItemModel(hookItem)) oriented along dir. Implement a vine chain as a green twisted strip. Move the keybind hint into the tooltip system (an input hint line) instead of the description.

findings.title: Potions and consumables: every use is 'drink', no quick-use keys, stack sizes mixed between versions
findings.evidence: Potions have maxStack 30 (lesser_healing_potion, swiftness_potion) and boss summons 20, but life_crystal and mana_crystal have 9999, a mix of pre-1.4.4 and 1.4.4 values. input.json has no quick_heal, quick_mana or quick_buff action. The tooltip shows 'Restores 50 life' but no buff duration (a swiftness potion with 14400 ticks says nothing). wooden_crate says 'Right click to open.' but right-click in the inventory splits the stack. In first person, drinking is just a 0.08 m lift.
findings.terraria_reference: H quick-heals, J quick-mana and B quick-buffs. In 1.4.4 potions, summons and crystals stack to 9999. Tooltips show '4 minute duration'. Right-click opens crates and bags and equips armor. Drinking raises the bottle to the face; food uses an eat style with crumbs.
findings.fix: Add input actions quick_heal (H), quick_mana (J) and quick_buff (B), calling a new ItemUseSystem.QuickUse(p, predicate) that picks the best backpack stack and runs Consume without changing the selection. Set maxStack to 9999 for potions and boss summons. In ItemTooltip, append `${ticks/3600} minute duration` when item.Buff != null. In SlotActions.RightClick: if the item has Consume.Loot, open it; if it has an EquipSlot, equip it; otherwise split. Give the first-person ViewModel a drink pose that tilts the bottle toward the camera.

findings.title: Armor and most accessories are invisible on the character
findings.evidence: The avatar attaches only the held item (hand.R) and wings. Rocket-boot flames and the double-jump puff are particles. Nothing reads Inventory.Armor or shields/balloons/boots for visuals (grep finds armor only in InventoryScreen). The helmet, chest_armor and greaves generators make standalone lathe props used only for icons. There are no vanity slots.
findings.terraria_reference: Every armor piece visibly changes the head, body and legs. Set bonuses have visual effects (e.g. glowing eyes). Shields, balloons and boots show on the character. Vanity and dye slots exist.
findings.fix: Add a PlayerAvatar.Armor partial. Short term: attach the helmet GLB to the 'head' bone, chest pieces to 'chest' with pauldrons on clavicle.L/R, greaves to the shins, shields to forearm.L, balloons tethered to the spine. Long term: generate skinned armor garments per armor set in tools/blender/bgen/human/garments.py (assets.json 'wearable' entries keyed by armorSet) and swap them in through CreatureVisual.SetAppearance.

findings.title: Blocks: held as an unlit flat icon card and placed with the generic 'use' lift
findings.evidence: ItemModel returns null for PlaceBlock items. In third person the block becomes a Sprite3D of the isometric-cube icon (0.25 m) rotated 90 degrees about X, a flat card. In first person the Sprite3D is Shaded = false, so a held dirt block is full-bright in a dark cave. Derived block items (UseStyle.Place, UseTime 12, UseAnimation 12) play 'use' (item lifted forward).
findings.terraria_reference: Placing tiles swings the item (style 1, useTime 10/useAnimation 15) and the tile sprite is held in the hand.
findings.fix: Build a 0.22 m cube mesh per block using the terrain material (texture-array layer from BlockDef) and cache it in PropLibrary.BlockCube(blockId). Use it for held (both views, lit via voxel_light) and dropped block items. Add a short 'place' swing clip and map UseStyle.Place to it.

findings.title: Rarity colours stop at tier 8: 52 lunar/endgame items show as yellow
findings.evidence: Rarity switch: 0 white, 1 (150,150,255), 2 (150,255,150), 3 (255,200,150), 4 (255,150,150), 5 (255,150,255), 6 (210,160,255), 7 (150,255,10), `_ => (1,1,0.04)`. Tiers 0-8 match Terraria exactly, but 48 items at rarity 10 (Solar Flare/Vortex/Nebula/Stardust gear, luminite_bar) and 4 at rarity 9 (fragments) all render in tier-8 yellow. Tier -1 is 0.6 grey (153) instead of 130. There are no Expert, Master or Quest rarities.
findings.terraria_reference: 9 Cyan (5,200,255), 10 Red (255,40,100), 11 Purple (180,40,255); Expert (-12) cycles rainbow; Master (-13) fiery red/orange; Quest (-11) amber (255,175,0); Gray (-1) (130,130,130).
findings.fix: Extend UiTheme.Rarity with 9, 10 and 11, and add sentinel values -11/-12/-13 with animated colours (pass Time.GetTicksMsec for the rainbow/fiery pulse and redraw hovered tooltips each frame). Document the values in ItemDef.Rarity and validate the range in ContentValidator.Items.

findings.title: Dropped items are flat, barely animated billboards with no rarity glow or light
findings.evidence: Each drop is a Y-billboard quad of the icon, size 0.3 (blocks) or 0.38. Bob is 0.05 + 0.04*sin(2.5t) and only when grounded. There is no spin. glow = rarity > 0 ? 0.08 : 0, which multiplies the icon's own colour rather than the rarity colour. Drops never emit light (fallen stars and torches on the ground are dark). All drops obey Gravity 20 (souls cannot float). There is no hover name or stack readout. MagnetRange 3.2 m and the pull speed of 9 m/s are fine.
findings.terraria_reference: Coins spin (animated sprite) and sparkle. Fallen Stars, souls and other ItemNoGravity/ItemIconPulse items float, pulse and give off light. Rare drops glint with their rarity colour so they are easy to spot. Hovering a drop shows its name and stack.
findings.fix: Render drops that have a GLB (manifest.json has 660) as the 3D model at about 0.35 scale, spinning at about 1.5 rad/s and bobbing at all times; use the block cube from the blocks finding for blocks; keep the billboard as a fallback. Add a shader instance param glow_color = UiTheme.Rarity(rarity) * (0.12 + 0.06*sin) for rarity ≥ 1, plus a small additive halo quad. Add pooled OmniLights (cap about 16) for items with HeldLight or tag 'glows'. Add an ItemDef.NoGravity flag honoured in DroppedItemSystem.Tick for souls and stars. Hover label: raycast the crosshair against drops within 4 m and show 'Name (count)'.

findings.title: Pickup feedback is a corner toast, not Terraria's world pop-up
findings.evidence: The Hud shows a right-aligned toast `+{stack.Count} {DisplayName}`, 2.2 s plus a 0.6 s fade, capped at 6 lines, and shared with refusal messages. Mining 30 dirt makes 30 '+1 Dirt Block' lines that push each other out. The prefix is omitted (DisplayName only). Coins show as '+37 Copper Coin'. The pickup and coin sounds already exist (good).
findings.terraria_reference: PopupText rises above the player's head as 'Copper Ore (5)' in the rarity colour. Repeated pickups of the same item within about 2 s merge and bump the count with a scale pop. Coins merge into a value line ('1 gold 23 silver'). The prefixed name is shown ('Legendary Muramasa').
findings.fix: Add game/UI/PickupText.cs: a small pool of Label3D (billboard, no depth test, outline) or screen-projected Labels anchored at player.Center + 2 m, keyed by (item, prefix) with coins sharing one key. On ItemPickedUp, if the key exists and is younger than 2 s, add the count, reset the timer and play a 1.25x scale tween; otherwise spawn a new label. Text is `{Prefix} {Name} ({n})` or Coins.Format(total) with per-denomination colours, and each label rises 0.6 m and fades. Keep toasts for system messages only.

findings.title: Coins never auto-convert; no coin slots; coins look like pancakes and don't spin
findings.evidence: Copper, silver and gold coins have maxStack 100 and platinum 9999. Inventory.Add merges into existing stacks and then empty slots, so 250 copper fills three slots (100/100/50) and never becomes 2 silver 50 copper. Denominations are consolidated only when spending (Wallet.TrySpend removes all coins and re-gives change). PlayerInventory has only a 50-slot backpack plus armor and accessories, with no coin (or ammo) slots. The inventory shows coins as the text '1 gold 20 silver'. The coin model is 3 stacked flat discs; the copper coin icon reads as a brown pancake stack.
findings.terraria_reference: 100 of a coin automatically becomes 1 of the next denomination on pickup or stacking. There are 4 dedicated coin slots, and coins are drawn as spinning animated sprites with the denomination's shine. The savings readout uses coin icons.
findings.fix: Add Coins.Normalize(Inventory) that recomputes Total and re-gives it in the largest denominations (reuse Wallet.Give logic), and call it from PlayerInventory.Pickup when stack.Item has tag 'coin'. Add `Inventory Coins = new(4)` and `Inventory Ammo = new(4)` to PlayerInventory, route coin pickups to Coins first, and make Coins.Total and Wallet use both inventories (update save/load). Render coins as a single thick disc with an embossed face and a spinning drop animation (see the dropped-items finding), and show the purse as coin icons with counts.

findings.title: Ammo: no ammo slots or selection order, no ammo count on the weapon, per-weapon ammo saving not implemented
findings.evidence: FindAmmo scans backpack slots 0..49, so hotbar ammo is used first and the player cannot choose. One ammo is consumed per trigger, correctly including the 4-pellet Boomstick. Ammo saving uses only the player stat AmmoSave (the Necro set's 0.2). The Megashark's '50% chance to not consume ammo' is description-only; there is no item field, and the Minishark's 33% is also missing. ItemSlotView draws s.Count only when > 1, so a gun slot never shows how many bullets are left.
findings.terraria_reference: The 4 ammo slots are consumed first, top to bottom, then the main inventory. The weapon's hotbar slot shows the total count of usable ammo. Megashark (50%), Minishark (33%) and others have built-in ammo conservation.
findings.fix: Add ItemDef.AmmoSaveChance and use `rng.Chance(stat + item.AmmoSaveChance)` in ItemUseSystem.Shoot. FindAmmo should search PlayerInventory.Ammo (4 slots, see the coins finding) and then Backpack. In ItemSlotView._Draw, when Item.UseAmmo != null, draw Inventory.Count(d => d.AmmoClass == UseAmmo) bottom-left in a smaller font (red when 0). Show mana-cost weapons greyed when out of mana.

findings.title: Prefixes: invented names, tooltips ignore prefix stats, sell price disagrees with the shop
findings.evidence: There are 18 prefixes. Some match Terraria (Keen, Ruthless, Broken, Sluggish, Lucky); the rest are invented: Stout, Brisk (a universal +10% speed, but Brisk is Terraria's +1% move-speed accessory prefix), Towering, Stubby, Mythic, Farsighted, Unerring, Transcendent, Sturdy, Fleet, Deft; and Arcane is a magic weapon prefix (+20 mana, +10% damage) instead of Terraria's accessory. The tooltip uses item.Damage, item.Crit, item.UseAnimation and item.Knockback, not Prefixes.*, and has no '+15% damage' lines. Sell price is item.Value/5, but the real sale is Prefixes.Value * 0.2. The held-name label and pickup toast drop the prefix. Reforging exists (TownServices.Reforge) but the plan still says it doesn't. The Bomb tooltip reads '70 generic damage' (damageType generic). A set bonus is shown even when the set isn't worn.
findings.terraria_reference: About 83 prefixes, e.g. Legendary (+15% dmg, +10% speed, +5% crit, +10% size, +15% kb), Godly, Demonic, Unreal, Mythical; accessories Warding (+4 def), Menacing (+4% dmg), Lucky (+4% crit), Quick (+4% move), Arcane (+20 mana). Tooltips show prefix-modified stats with green/red modifier lines, the player-adjusted damage, and the set bonus only when the set is worn.
findings.fix: Replace the combat.json prefixes with Terraria's full table and values, grouped as universal/common, melee, ranged, magic and accessory (move to data/prefixes.json). In ItemTooltip, use Prefixes.Damage/Crit/Knockback/UseTime(stack), add TooltipKind.Modifier lines ('+15% damage', green if positive and red if negative, coloured in ItemSlotView), show the sell price from Prefixes.Value * SellRatio, print 'N damage' for Generic, and show SetBonus only when PlayerInventory.CompleteSet() includes the item. Use the prefixed name in Hud._heldName and the pickup text. Update MASTER_PLAN lines 76 and 98.

findings.title: Icons: soft 3D renders with no outline; guns seen from underneath; tiers share one silhouette
findings.evidence: Icons are 128 px Cycles renders (24 samples) under two sun lights, with no outline or posterisation. The 'item' view camera looks along direction (0,-1,0.05) at the model tilted 45 degrees, but the gun generator puts the grip, receiver and barrel height on +Y. Every gun icon (minishark, flintlock_pistol, sniper_rifle) is therefore seen from below as a dark stick. The whip coil renders as a black zigzag, and spear heads come out black. The pickaxe/axe/hammer generators take only a tint: the 17 '{metal}_pickaxe' patterns plus the lunar pickaxes share one silhouette (copper vs gold differ only in colour). The slot draws the icon inside a 14% inset (72% of the slot).
findings.terraria_reference: Crisp pixel-art sprites with a dark 1-2 px outline, saturated palette and strong silhouette. Each ore tier's tools, bows and swords have distinct shapes; guns are drawn in side profile.
findings.fix: In render_icon, pick the view per generator: guns and launchers from +X (side profile, barrel pointing right-up); whips from an uncoiled S-curve pose; spears with the head lit. Add a stylisation pass: a Freestyle line or compositor alpha-dilate for a 2 px dark outline, a toon ramp (Shader-to-RGB with a constant ramp) and slight posterisation, keeping 128 px for sharp downsampling. Add shape params per tier to the pickaxe/axe/hammer/sword/bow generators (head curve, spikes, blade profile) and put them in assets.json metals as a 'style' table. Draw the icon at about 80% of the slot.

findings.title: Autoswing: every melee weapon auto-repeats and the data flag is dead for melee
findings.evidence: `repeats = item.AutoReuse || info.IsTool || Place* || Melee || Thrust` (commented 'every sword auto-swings, as in 1.4.4'). Ranged and magic items honour autoReuse: Flintlock Pistol, Boomstick and Sniper Rifle are click-per-shot; Minishark and Megashark are held. Whips also auto-repeat because they are Melee. The autoReuse values in the data are inconsistent: wooden_sword has none and muramasa has true, but neither matters for melee. Feral Claws is only '+12% melee speed'.
findings.terraria_reference: In 1.4.4 most melee weapons autoswing. Whips and some others need Feral Claws or its upgrades, which 'enable auto swing for melee weapons and whips'. Guns follow per-item autoReuse.
findings.fix: Keep the behaviour, but have the validator reject autoReuse on melee items (or normalise it) so the flag is not dead data. Exclude whips from forced repeat and add an 'autoswing' stat effect to feral_claws and its upgrades that enables it. If autoswing is shown in tooltips at all, show it consistently.

summary:
Strata's in-game UI covers a lot already: a 10-slot hotbar, a 50-slot backpack, 3 armor and 5 accessory slots, chest Loot all/Deposit all, a crafting list, tooltips (the speed and knockback words match Terraria's thresholds exactly), a boss bar, big announcements, 3D damage numbers, a minimap and full map, and a town dialog with services. It still looks like a generic dark-slate Godot UI rather than Terraria. There is no font file at all (Godot's fallback font is used). Life and mana are plain progress bars, not hearts and stars. Buffs are text chips, not icons. Panels are a desaturated near-black navy instead of Terraria's translucent royal blue (63,82,151) at 70% alpha, and the hotbar sits bottom-centre like Minecraft. Several correctness bugs also hurt polish:
- Tooltips ignore prefix stats and prefix value.
- Rarity 9 and 10 items (51 in data) show as yellow.
- The crafting list rebuilds every 0.5 s, which destroys its own tooltips (the only place ingredients are shown).
- Tooltips set on Labels (shop rows, buff row) can never appear.
- Layouts use absolute pixels and collide: crafting panel over the minimap below 1340 logical px, buff row over the FPS label, info text over the F3 overlay, shop dialog pushed past the bottom edge.
Missing Terraria features: coin/ammo slots, a saved trash slot, sort/quick stack/favourites, vanity/dye/misc equipment, crafting with material slots and hold-to-craft, a grid shop with sell-by-click, a chat log using Terraria's status colours, pickup popup text, a custom and smart cursor, and a housing query UI. Quickest high-impact wins: one global theme plus a font, the Terraria palette, hearts/stars, buff icons, the tooltip prefix and rarity fixes, and stopping the crafting list rebuild.

findings.title: Panel/slot palette is dark slate, not Terraria's translucent royal-blue skin
findings.evidence: PanelColor=(0.07,0.09,0.14,0.86), PanelBorder=(0.35,0.45,0.65,0.9), border 2px, radius 6; SlotColor=(0.14,0.19,0.32,0.82), SlotBorder=(0.32,0.42,0.66,0.95); selected = gold border (1,0.86,0.35) width 3 only; hover = SlotColor.Lightened(0.15); Buttons reuse Panel(0.9) with 4px margins.

findings.title: Theme covers only 4 control types and must be attached per root; many widgets fall back to Godot defaults
findings.evidence: Build() sets only PanelContainer.panel, Label font_color/outline, Button normal/hover/pressed and TooltipPanel.panel. It has no styles for ProgressBar, V/HScrollBar (crafting and shop scroll lists), TabContainer/TabBar, CheckButton, HSlider, OptionButton/PopupMenu or LineEdit. Button has no 'disabled' or 'focus' style, yet crafting rows use Disabled=true. project.godot has no [gui] section. Theme is assigned by hand at Hud.cs:44, InventoryScreen.cs:40, TownDialog.cs:36, WorldMapScreen.cs:36/42, SettingsScreen.cs:24, PerfOverlay.cs:23 and MenuKit.cs:38/56/65/103/112/137. The console panel, pause backdrop and minimap never get it.
findings.terraria_reference: One uniform skin everywhere: blue translucent panels, thin rounded blue scrollbars (dark-blue track, light-blue thumb), on/off icon toggles, colour-bar sliders with a knob, all text in Andy Bold with a black outline.
findings.fix:
Extend UiTheme.Build():
- VScrollBar/HScrollBar: 'scroll' = StyleBoxFlat Color8(20,26,60,170), radius 6, margins 4; 'grabber' = Color8(120,140,220); 'grabber_highlight' = Color8(160,180,255); 'grabber_pressed' = Color8(255,215,0); set the 'scroll_bar' width to 12.

- HSlider: 'slider' = 6px bar; 'grabber_area' = gold.
- CheckButton: checked/unchecked icon textures.
- OptionButton/PopupMenu: 'panel' = Panel(); 'hover' = Color8(73,94,171).
- LineEdit: 'normal' = Color8(20,24,50,200).
- Button: 'disabled' = Panel at alpha 0.4, with font_disabled_color (0.55,0.55,0.6).
Then export once with ResourceSaver.Save(UiTheme.Theme, "res://assets/ui/strata_theme.tres") (a console/tool command) and add [gui] theme/custom="res://assets/ui/strata_theme.tres" to project.godot. Every CanvasLayer (console, pause, minimap, main menu) then picks it up, and the scattered Theme= assignments can go.

findings.title: No UI font: everything uses Godot's fallback font instead of an Andy Bold-style face
findings.evidence: The repo has no .ttf/.otf/.fnt/.woff files. Theme is created with { DefaultFontSize = 15 } and no DefaultFont. MapView labels use ThemeDB.FallbackFont at 13px. Label3D damage numbers and NPC name tags have no Font set.

findings.title: Life and mana are progress bars, not hearts (golden past 400) and a stars column
findings.evidence: The vitals VBox (min width 260, TopRight, offset -16/14) holds ProgressBars of 260x22 with 4px-rounded fills: Life (0.86,0.18,0.22), Mana (0.22,0.45,0.95). Their text is "Life {Life}/{MaxLife}" and "Mana {Mana}/{MaxMana}" at 13px. BaseLife=100 and BaseMana=20 are exactly Terraria's starting values.
findings.terraria_reference: Classic style: 'Life: 100/100' above a row of 22x22 heart sprites (~26px pitch). 20 HP per heart, 10 per row, 2 rows maximum (20 hearts = 400). Past 400 max life, each Life Fruit (+5) turns one heart golden, and each heart then shows MaxLife/20 HP. The partially filled heart is drawn smaller and fainter; hearts pulse gently. Mana is a vertical column of stars at the far right edge: 20 mana per star, up to 10 stars (MaxMana/10 per star above 200), labelled 'Mana'. Version 1.4 also offers 'Fancy' and 'Bars' styles.
findings.fix:
Hud.cs is 373 lines (CI cap 400), so add a partial file Hud.Vitals.cs with two controls.

LifeHearts : Control, drawn in _Draw:
- lifePer = MaxLife>400 ? MaxLife/20f : 20
- count = min(20, ceil(MaxLife/lifePer))
- heart i is gold when i < (MaxLife-400)/5
- fill = clamp((Life - i*lifePer)/lifePer, 0, 1)
- draw at scale 0.6+0.4*fill with alpha 0.4+0.6*fill; 10 per row; 26px pitch
- the last full heart pulses at scale 1+0.04*sin(t*4)

ManaStars : Control: a vertical column, starPer = MaxMana>200 ? MaxMana/10f : 20.

Anchor the hearts TopRight at offset (-300,32) with a 'Life: X/Y' Label above them. Anchor the stars TopRight at (-28,30). Generate heart.png, heart_gold.png and star.png (22x22, pixel style) into assets/ui/ with a new tools/textures/build_ui.py. Keep the bars behind UserSettings.LifeDisplay ("classic"|"bars"), exposed as a MenuKit.Row in SettingsScreen.Interface (SettingsScreen.cs:131-140).

findings.title: Breath shown as a third bar (overlapping the minimap) instead of Terraria bubbles
findings.evidence: Breath is a 260x22 ProgressBar (0.55,0.85,1) with the text "Breath {n}%" or "Drowning!". MaxBreath is 1200 ticks. It is the vitals VBox's 3rd row (y 66..88, 4px separation), which overlaps the minimap frame at TopRight (-226,70). The HUD is on Layer 10 and the minimap on Layer 5, so the bar covers the top of the map.
findings.terraria_reference: 10 bubble sprites above the player's head, each worth one tenth of breath (breathMax 200). Bubbles pop one by one and are hidden when breath is full.
findings.fix: Add BreathBubbles : Control in Hud.Vitals.cs, anchored CenterBottom just above the held-item name (or under the crosshair). Draw 10 bubbles of 18px; bubble i is drawn when breath > i*MaxBreath/10, and the partial bubble is scaled by its fraction. Flash red (Color8(255,80,90)) when breath is 0. Remove _breath and _breathText from the vitals column.

findings.title: Hotbar: bottom-centre Minecraft layout, no selected-slot scale, fading name, shown twice while the inventory is open
findings.evidence: 10 fixed 58px slots, separation 4, anchored CenterBottom at OffsetBottom -14. Selection only swaps to a 3px gold border. The held-item name sits at OffsetBottom -90 and fades out after 2.5s (_heldNameTime = 2.5f, Modulate alpha clamp). The HUD hotbar stays visible while the inventory is open, and the backpack grid's first row is the same 10 slots, so the hotbar appears twice (see docs/screenshots/m1_inventory.png). Bows and guns show no ammo count.
findings.terraria_reference: The hotbar is top-left. Unselected slots are drawn at ~0.75 scale and the selected slot eases to 1.0 (Main.hotbarScale lerp) with the gold Inventory_Back14 fill. The selected item's prefix+name is printed above the hotbar at all times, and reads 'Inventory' when the inventory is open. When the inventory opens, the hotbar simply becomes row 1 of the 10x5 grid. Ranged weapons show the ammo count in their slot.
findings.fix: Add UserSettings.HotbarPosition: "top_left" (default, Terraria) or "bottom_center" (first-person friendly). In Hud._Process, keep a per-slot scale with _scale[i] = Mathf.MoveToward(_scale[i], sel ? 1f : 0.78f, (float)delta*3f) and apply it via ItemSlotView.Scale with PivotOffset = Size/2. Make the name label persistent, rarity-coloured and prefix-aware. When the inventory opens, set hotbar.Visible = false and show 'Inventory' in the name label; place InventoryScreen's grid so its row 1 lands exactly where the hotbar was. In ItemSlotView add Func<int>? AmmoCount and draw it bottom-right when item.UseAmmo != null, summing matching stacks with the ItemUseSystem.FindAmmo logic.

findings.title: Inventory screen uses absolute pixel positions; panels collide and don't reflow with UI scale
findings.evidence: Panels sit at fixed positions: backpack (24,24); equipment (24+10*54+40 = 604, 24); chest (24, 24+5*54+40 = 334); crafting (24+540+40+180 = 784, 96) at min 330x420, so its right edge is x=1114. The minimap (Layer 5, TopRight, x W-226..W-16, y 70..280) is not hidden while the inventory is open (show = ShowMinimap && !_full.IsOpen && Alive). So at any logical width under 1340px (a 1280x720 window, or 1600 wide at UI scale 1.2 or more, since ContentScaleFactor divides it) the crafting panel covers the minimap. The older screenshot docs/screenshots/m1_inventory.png shows the same kind of overlap with the life/mana bars. No containers or anchors are used, so nothing reflows.
findings.terraria_reference: A fixed, anchored arrangement: inventory top-left (hotbar = row 1); coin and ammo columns to its right; chest or shop directly under the inventory; crafting column at the bottom-left; equipment column on the right edge under the minimap, with the defense shield beside it and tab icons (Equipment/Misc/Housing/Camera) underneath. Hearts and minimap are never covered.
findings.fix: Rebuild the layout with containers: root MarginContainer(FullRect, margins 20) -> HBoxContainer[ left VBox (backpack+coin/ammo HBox, chest/shop panel, CraftingPanel with SizeFlagsVertical=ExpandFill) | Control spacer ExpandFill | right VBox (equipment, defense, tabs) with top margin 70+210+8 so it starts under the minimap ]. Pass the crafting panel's size from layout instead of a hard-coded Vector2. Split into InventoryScreen.cs, InventoryScreen.Layout.cs and InventoryScreen.Equipment.cs to stay under the 400-line cap.

findings.title: No coin slots or ammo slots; coins shown as a plain 'N copper' label
findings.evidence: PlayerInventory only has Backpack(50), Armor(3), Accessories(5) and Cursor. Coins take backpack slots and are summed into a Label via Coins.Format ("0 copper" in the screenshot), shown under the trash slot. FindAmmo scans the whole backpack.
findings.terraria_reference: Two narrow columns right of the 10x5 grid: 4 coin slots and 4 ammo slots, drawn at ~0.6 scale with 'Coins' and 'Ammo' captions. Picked-up coins go to the coin slots first and auto-convert (100 of a tier becomes the next tier). Ammo is used from the ammo slots first, top to bottom.
findings.fix: In the core, add Inventory Coins = new(4) and Inventory Ammo = new(4) to PlayerInventory, with filters Category==ItemCategory.Coin and AmmoClass!=null. Pickup() routes coins to Coins, then the backpack; ammo goes to Ammo when a matching stack exists or a slot is free. Coins.Total sums Coins+Backpack. FindAmmo searches Ammo first. Save both in the player file. In InventoryScreen, add two VBoxContainers of 4 ItemSlotViews at size 34 (SlotKind.Coin/Ammo), each under a 14px caption. Remove the _coins text label.

findings.title: Trash slot is unsaved, misplaced, and shift-click silently trashes items
findings.evidence: _trash = new Inventory(1) is a field of the UI object, not part of PlayerInventory, so its contents are lost on exit. It sits in the equipment column under a 'Trash' Label. With no chest open, shift-click on any non-equippable backpack item moves it to the trash (QuickMove(backpack, index, _trash), line 206). ItemSlotView.EmptyHint exists but is never assigned anywhere.
findings.terraria_reference: Trash is at the bottom-right corner of the inventory grid with a faint trash-can silhouette. It is saved with the player. Ctrl+Click trashes an item; Shift+Click quick-moves it to a chest or equips it.
findings.fix: Move Trash into PlayerInventory and save it. Render it at the grid's bottom-right with EmptyHint = GD.Load<Texture2D>("res://assets/ui/trash.png"). Extend ItemSlotView.Clicked to (button, shift, ctrl). In InventoryScreen.Slot, ctrl sends the item to the trash and shift only quick-moves or equips.

findings.title: Chest/inventory management buttons missing: sort, quick stack, restock, rename, favourites
findings.evidence: The chest header only has framed 'Loot all' and 'Deposit all' Buttons. The chest title is obj.Def.DisplayName and cannot be renamed. There is no Sort, Quick Stack, Restock, inventory Sort, 'quick stack to nearby chests', or Alt+click favourite. SlotActions only offers LeftClick, RightClick, QuickMove, Stow and filters.

findings.title: Equipment panel is bare: no silhouettes, no vanity/dye/misc slots, text defense, fixed 5 accessories

- Replace _defense with a DefenseBadge : Control that draws a 36px shield texture with the number centred in 16px outlined text.

- Add a TabBar of 32px icon buttons (Equipment | Misc | Housing).

findings.title: Crafting panel rebuilds every 0.5 s (killing its own tooltips); text list instead of slots, materials, cursor output and hold-to-craft
findings.evidence: _Process calls Refresh() every 0.5 s while visible (_refreshTimer = 0.5). Refresh QueueFree()s and recreates every row Button. The hovered row's tooltip, the only place ingredients appear (Describe(): 'Requires:\n  2x Wood\nAt: workbench', plain text), is destroyed under the mouse, and hover highlight flickers. Browse lists uncraftable recipes as disabled rows. A click crafts once into the backpack. Shift crafts MaxStack/Count at once (line 75). Rows are 300x40 Buttons with a 32px icon.
findings.terraria_reference: A crafting column at the bottom-left: a vertical strip of item slots for recipes craftable now, scrolled with the mouse wheel. The selected recipe is enlarged, with its required materials as a row of small slots and 'Required Objects: Work Bench'. A click puts the result on the mouse cursor (repeat clicks stack). Holding right-click crafts repeatedly, speeding up. A hammer toggle shows a grid of everything craftable.
findings.fix:
Keep a signature of the Browse result, e.g. string.Join over (recipe id, CanCraft, MaxCrafts). Rebuild only when it changes; otherwise update counts in place.

Replace the Buttons with ItemSlotView rows inside the ScrollContainer. The selected recipe shows an HBox of 32px ingredient ItemSlotViews (count text red when short), with 'Requires: Work Bench' below.

Craft into _ui.Inventory.Cursor: merge when it holds the same item, refuse when it holds another.

Hold-to-craft in _Process: while the right mouse button is held over the selected recipe, craft every interval = max(0.05, 0.4 - 0.05*crafted) seconds.

Hide uncraftable recipes behind a 'Show all' toggle.

findings.title: Tooltips ignore prefix stats and value; no green/red modifier lines, coin colours, instant follow-cursor display
findings.evidence: The name line includes the prefix (line 20), but the stats read the raw ItemDef: item.Damage, 4 + item.Crit, Speed(item.UseAnimation), Knockback(item.Knockback), item.ManaCost, item.Defense. The sell price is item.Value/5 (line 42), not Prefixes.Value(stack). There are no '+10% damage' lines. The price prints as one-colour 'Sell price: 1 silver 20 copper' (0.95,0.85,0.5); a zero value prints nothing. The stack count is not in the name. Godot's default tooltip delay (0.5 s) applies because project.godot has no gui/timers/tooltip_delay_sec, and the tooltip does not follow the mouse. Note: the Speed and Knockback word tables (lines 47-70) already match Terraria's thresholds exactly.
findings.terraria_reference:
Lines in order:
- Name in rarity colour, with prefix and '(25)' stack count.
- Stats: '42 melee damage', '8% critical strike chance', 'Very fast speed', 'Strong knockback'.
- Info lines: 'Equipable', '5 defense', 'Consumable', 'Material', then flavour text.
- Prefix lines: '+10% damage', '-5% speed' and so on, green (120,190,120) when good and red (190,120,120) when bad.
- 'Sell price' coloured by its top coin: platinum (220,220,198), gold (224,201,92), silver (181,192,193), copper (246,138,96); grey 'No value' when zero.

The tooltip appears instantly and follows the cursor.
findings.fix:
In ItemTooltip.Lines, use Prefixes.Damage(stack), Prefixes.Crit(stack), Speed(Prefixes.UseTime(stack, item.UseAnimation)), Knockback(Prefixes.Knockback(stack)), Prefixes.ManaCost(stack) and Prefixes.Value(stack).

Add TooltipKind.Good, Bad and Coin. Emit one line per non-zero PrefixDef field (Damage, UseSpeed, Crit, Knockback, Size, Velocity, ManaCost with the sign inverted, Defense, MoveSpeed, MaxMana), formatted like $"{v*100:+0;-0}% damage".

Name line: '{name} ({count})' when count > 1. Show 'No value' when the value is 0.

In ItemSlotView, map Good to Color8(120,190,120), Bad to Color8(190,120,120), and Coin to the top coin's colour.

Add [gui] timers/tooltip_delay_sec=0.0 to project.godot. Better: a single TooltipFollower Control on its own CanvasLayer (Layer 60) that ItemSlotViews fill on MouseEntered and clear on MouseExited, positioned at mouse+(16,16) each frame and clamped to the viewport.

findings.title: Rarity colours wrong for tiers 9 and 10 (51 items) and missing -11/-12/-13 special tiers
findings.evidence: The fallback `_ => new Color(1f,1f,0.04f)` makes rarity 9 (4 items) and rarity 10 (47 items) the same yellow as rarity 8. Negative rarities use (0.6,0.6,0.6), i.e. grey 153. Tiers 1-8 match Terraria.
findings.fix: Add switch arms: 9 => Color.Color8(5,200,255); 10 => Color8(255,40,100); 11 => Color8(180,40,255); -1 => Color8(130,130,130); -11 => Color8(255,175,0). For -12 use Color.FromHsv((Time.GetTicksMsec()/1000f*0.3f)%1f, 0.6f, 1f). For -13 use Color8(255,(byte)(120+80*Mathf.Sin(t*4)),0). Animated tiers need re-colouring in _Process for the name label and tooltip. Optionally add Prefixes.Rarity(stack) to shift the tier by prefix quality.

findings.title: Buff row is text chips: no icons, no working hover, no cancel, overlaps the FPS label
findings.evidence: Each buff is a PanelContainer with a Label like "Regeneration 23s" in BuffDef.Color, placed at (16,14). BuffDef.Icon exists but nothing reads it, and there are no buff icon assets. label.TooltipText (line 265) can never show: Godot Labels ignore the mouse by default, and the mouse is captured during gameplay. With 8+8 content margins the row spans y 14..~51 and overlaps the FPS label at (16,44). No right-click cancel. AddThemeColorOverride runs on every label every frame.
findings.terraria_reference: Rows of 32x32 buff icons (about 11 per row) under the hotbar, each with a small timer below ('30 s', '5 m', none for permanent buffs). With the inventory open, hovering shows the name and description, and right-clicking cancels a buff (not a debuff). Debuff icons look distinct.
findings.fix: New game/UI/BuffBar.cs: an HFlowContainer of BuffIconView : Control (min 32x46). Each view draws a cached texture from res://assets/icons/buffs/{Icon??Id}.png. Until icons exist, fall back to a rounded square in BuffDef.Color with the first letter, and a 2px red border when Debuff. Timer text is t<60 ? $"{t} s" : t<3600 ? $"{t/60} m" : $"{t/3600} h", hidden when Persistent. findings.title: Combat text: no heal/mana numbers, non-Terraria colours, no pop animation, default font
findings.evidence: Label3D numbers (FontSize 56, 72 on crit; PixelSize 0.005; outline 14; NoDepthTest) rise 1.1 m over 0.9 s. Colours: damage to player (1,0.3,0.3), crit (1,0.6,0.15), normal (1,0.9,0.45). Only NPC and town damage raise events. Potions call Vitals.Heal with no event, so there are no green or blue numbers. No scale pop.
findings.terraria_reference: CombatText colours: damage to enemies (255,160,80); crits (255,100,30), bigger and with a slight shake; damage to the player (255,80,90); life heal (100,255,100); mana (100,100,255). Text pops in (scale 0->1), rises with decaying velocity and fades.
findings.fix: Core: add an event Healed(PlayerEntity, int amount, bool mana) raised in ItemUseSystem where HealLife and HealMana are applied (~line 260). CombatEffects subscribes and calls Number(kind). Colours: Color8(255,160,80), Color8(255,100,30), Color8(255,80,90), Color8(100,255,100), Color8(100,100,255). Tween Scale from 0.3 to 1 over 0.08 s with TransitionType.Back; crits get x1.25 scale and ±0.05 m x-jitter. Set label.Font to the UI font. Consider FixedSize=true with PixelSize ~0.0012 so numbers keep a constant screen size, as they do in 2D Terraria.

findings.title: Enemy health shown as red 'life/max' text instead of a small colour-shifting bar
findings.evidence: Damaged NPCs get a Label3D reading "{npc.Life}/{npc.MaxLife}" (FontSize 48, PixelSize 0.004, Modulate (1,0.45,0.45)) above the head.
findings.terraria_reference: A small health bar (~36px sprite) just below a damaged enemy, sliding green -> yellow -> red with the life fraction. No numbers; the name and life appear only in the mouse-over text.
findings.fix: Replace the Health Label3D with a MeshInstance3D QuadMesh (0.8x0.1 m) using a shared billboard, unshaded ShaderMaterial with an instance uniform float fraction. Colour = fraction>0.5 ? mix(yellow, green, (f-0.5)*2) : mix(red, yellow, f*2), with a dark 1px border. Set it per view with SetInstanceShaderParameter("fraction", life/max). Show numbers only for the crosshair target via Hud._targetName ('Zombie 34/45').

findings.title: Boss bar: top-centre plain bar without boss icon or life numbers
findings.evidence: A PanelContainer 520px wide at CenterTop (OffsetTop 14) holds an 18px title Label and a 500x18 ProgressBar with fill (0.75,0.12,0.2). The life Label that Bar() returns is thrown away (`(_bossBar, _) = Bar(...)`, line 128), so no numbers are shown. BossInfo has Title, Flag and Music but no icon.
findings.terraria_reference: Version 1.4 draws the boss bar at the bottom-centre: an ornate frame sprite, the boss head icon at the left end, a red fill with a lighter top highlight, and 'current/max' life centred on the bar. Paired or multi-part bosses combine into one bar; shields get a secondary bar.
findings.fix:
Add string? Icon to BossInfo (default = enemy id) and head icons under assets/icons/bosses/. New game/UI/BossBar.cs, anchored CenterBottom above the hotbar (OffsetBottom -100), or CenterTop if the hotbar is moved to the bottom:
- 40x40 icon TextureRect.
- A _Draw bar 456x22: background Color8(30,10,20,200); fill Color8(200,30,50); 3px top highlight Color8(255,120,120,160); 2px black frame.
- A centred 14px Label '{life}/{max}'.
- A trailing 'damage chunk' in Color8(255,200,200,180) that MoveToward()s the real value after a 0.4 s delay.

findings.title: Status messages are big centred banners with non-Terraria colours; no chat log
findings.evidence: Every world message (boss awoken/defeated/left, NPC arrived/slain/left, events, objectives, progression) is a 30px centred Label at OffsetTop 120. Each shows 4 s, fades over 1.5 s, and at most 4 stack. Colours: awoken (0.8,0.5,1) = (204,128,255); arrived (0.55,0.9,0.6), green; slain (1,0.4,0.35). There is no message history. The console (` / F1) is developer-only, near-black (0.04,0.05,0.07,0.88).
findings.terraria_reference: Messages print to the chat log at the bottom-left (~16px Andy Bold, outlined). Each line lives ~10 s (chatLength 600 ticks), then fades; up to 10 lines show. Enter opens chat with history. Colours: '<Boss> has awoken!' and 'has been defeated!' (175,75,255); '<NPC> has arrived!' (50,125,255); '<NPC> was slain...' (255,25,25); events such as 'The Blood Moon is rising...' (50,255,130).
findings.fix: New game/UI/ChatLog.cs: a VBoxContainer anchored BottomLeft at offset (80,-120), holding RichTextLabel lines (FitContent, 16px, outline 4). AddLine(text, color) fades each line after 10 s and keeps at most 10. Route Hud.Announce() into it; keep a smaller (24px) centred banner only for boss awoken/defeated if wanted. Colours: Color8(175,75,255), Color8(50,125,255), Color8(255,25,25), Color8(50,255,130). Optional: Enter opens a themed LineEdit that sends '/' commands to the existing CommandRegistry via DebugConsole.Run, so the console doubles as Terraria-style chat.

findings.title: Item pickups appear as right-edge toasts instead of popup text above the player
findings.evidence: The ItemPickedUp handler calls Toast("+{Count} {DisplayName}") with the rarity colour into a CenterRight VBox (OffsetRight -24). Each toast holds 2.2 s, fades over 0.6 s; at most 6.
findings.terraria_reference: PopupText above the player's head: 'Wood (37)' in rarity colour, rising and fading over ~1-2 s. Repeated pickups of the same item merge into one popup whose count grows with a scale bump. Coins read '1 gold 20 silver' in coin colour.
findings.fix: Add a PickupText manager (game/Entities, reusing the CombatEffects Label3D pool). Alternatively use a Hud-level Label positioned with Camera3D.UnprojectPosition(head + 0.4 m). Keep Dictionary<itemId, (label, total, timer)>; a repeat within 1.5 s adds to total, restarts the fade, and tweens Scale 1.3 -> 1.0 over 0.12 s. Text is '{name} ({total})' in UiTheme.Rarity. Keep right-edge toasts only for refusals and errors.

findings.title: NPC chat and shop: bottom-anchored box that spills off-screen, framed buttons, list shop, dead tooltips, sell-held-only
findings.evidence: A 560px panel anchored CenterBottom at offset (-280,-330), growing downward. With the 190px shop scroll visible the box is about 350px tall, so it runs ~20px past the bottom edge and over the hotbar. Actions are framed Buttons (Shop/Heal/Help/Quest/Chat/Close). Shop rows are [32px icon, name Label, price Label, 'Buy' Button]. The item tooltip is set on the name Label (line 148), which ignores the mouse, so it never appears. Selling is only 'Sell held stack' (the selected hotbar slot). Reforge acts on the held item. The inventory is not opened alongside the shop.
findings.terraria_reference: The chat box sits at the top-centre (~500px, dark translucent blue Chat_Back with a light rim), with white wrapped text. Buttons are plain text ('Shop', 'Close', 'Happiness', service) that turn yellow and grow on hover. Shop opens the inventory plus a 10x4 (40-slot) shop grid where the chest goes. Click to buy ('Buy price' in the tooltip); right-click-hold buys stackables one by one. Sell with Shift/Ctrl-click or by dropping the cursor item onto the shop; buy-back slots list recent sales. Reforge shows a 'Place an item here to reforge' slot, the cost and a hammer button.
findings.fix:
Anchor _root CenterTop (OffsetTop 90, GrowVertical End) so it grows away from the hotbar. Use UiTheme.TextButton: 20px, hover colour Color8(255,215,0), Scale tween 1 -> 1.1.

Shop: add InventoryScreen.OpenShop(TownNpc). It opens the inventory and fills the chest area with a 10-column grid of read-only ItemSlotViews (SlotKind.Chest) whose tooltip appends 'Buy price: ...' in coin colours. A click buys into the Cursor via Commerce.Buy. While the shop is open, Shift/Ctrl-click on backpack slots calls a generalised Commerce.Sell(player, backpackIndex). Add a buy-back list to Commerce.

Reforge: a single ItemSlotView slot, a cost Label and a hammer Button.

findings.title: No custom cursor; Cursor Colour setting only tints the 3D outline; cursor item only inside the inventory
findings.evidence: The OS arrow shows whenever the mouse is free. CursorColor (default "#ffffff") is read only by TargetHighlight.Neutral. The crosshair is four 2px white lines (alpha 0.45, or 0.95 in reach). The held-stack icon (44px at mouse+6) and its count are drawn only by InventoryScreen, not over the TownDialog or other layers. There is no hover icon for NPCs, chests or doors.
findings.terraria_reference: A custom triangular pointer in the Cursor Colour (default pinkish red, approx (255,50,95)) with a Border Colour outline. The held mouse item is drawn next to the cursor on every screen. Hovering a town NPC shows a speech-bubble icon; hovering a chest shows the chest icon.
findings.fix: Generate assets/ui/cursor.png: a 16x16 white triangle with a 2px dark border. At boot and on UserSettings.Changed, tint it (Image.Duplicate, multiply by CursorColor) and call Input.SetCustomMouseCursor(ImageTexture.CreateFromImage(img), Input.CursorShape.Arrow, Vector2.Zero). Consider defaulting CursorColor to "#ff325f". Tint Hud.Crosshair the same way. When Interaction.Target is an NPC, container or door, draw a 20px icon and key hint ('E  Talk', 'E  Open') right of the crosshair. Move the cursor-stack TextureRect to a top-most CanvasLayer (Layer 90) so it follows the mouse over the shop, chest and dialogs.

findings.title: No smart cursor or auto-select; only 'Smart dig'
findings.evidence: 'Smart dig' means that looking steeply down (dir.Y <= -0.8) with a pickaxe targets the ground under your feet. input.json has no smart_cursor or auto_select action; Ctrl is crouch and Shift is sprint.
findings.terraria_reference: Left Ctrl toggles Smart Cursor: it targets the nearest relevant tile near the cursor (ore/blocks for pickaxes, trees for axes, walls for hammers) and lines up platforms and rope. Holding Left Shift is Auto Select: it temporarily switches to the right torch, pickaxe, axe, hammer, bucket or potion for what is under the cursor. Both are signalled on the HUD.
findings.fix:
Add 'smart_cursor' and 'auto_select' actions to input.json on free keys (e.g. key:X and mouse:3; Ctrl and Shift are taken), expose them in SettingsScreen.Controls, and add UserSettings.SmartCursor. In InteractionController:
- Smart mode: search a ~15° cone around Aim within reach and pick the first block the held tool can affect (PickPower >= hardness; trees for axes).
- Auto-select: while held, scan hotbar slots for the best tool for the current target, swap SelectedHotbar, and restore it on release.
- Toast 'Smart Cursor: On/Off' and tint the crosshair orange while active.

findings.title: No housing menu or query; no bestiary or emote buttons
findings.evidence: Housing.Scan(cell) returns a Room with Valid and a Problems list, but only console commands and probes use it. There is no housing tab, NPC banner list or '?' query in game/UI, and no bestiary or emote UI anywhere. TownSystem has no assign or evict API (grep for Assign/Home/Evict found nothing).
findings.terraria_reference: The Housing tab (house icon among the equipment tabs) lists town NPC head banners, which you drag onto a room to assign. The '?' query, clicked on a room, prints 'This housing is suitable.' or the exact problem ('This housing is missing a light source.'). Banners hang in assigned rooms. Bestiary (book) and emote (bubble) buttons sit near the crafting area.
findings.fix:
Add game/UI/HousingPanel.cs as a tab of the equipment column:
- A '?' Button enters query mode. The next use_primary on a cell calls _ui.Game.Housing.Scan(cell) and posts Problems[0], or 'This housing is suitable.', to ChatLog in Color8(255,240,20).
- A GridContainer of resident head icons (assets/icons/npcs/*.png) with a tooltip 'Lives at x,y' and right-click evict.
- Core: TownSystem.AssignHome(npc, room) and Evict(npc).
Bestiary and emote buttons are low priority; stubs are fine.

findings.title: Death screen is plain red text: no dim, no cause of death
findings.evidence: A FullRect Label at 44px in (0.9,0.25,0.25) reads "You were slain\nRespawning in {n}" (Hardcore: '... has perished'). There is no background dim or fade-in, and the core records no death reason.
findings.terraria_reference: The screen darkens. Large 'You were slain...' (FontDeathText, ~48px) appears with the cause beneath ('<Name> was slain by a Zombie.', also posted to chat), plus the respawn countdown.
findings.fix: Add a FullRect ColorRect behind the label that tweens from alpha 0 to 0.55 over 1 s. Title 'You were slain...' at 48px in Color8(225,25,25), with a second 20px Label for the cause. Core: store the last damage source name on PlayerEntity where NpcSystem hurts the player (line ~275), and post '<Name> was slain by <X>.' to ChatLog in the same colour.

findings.title: Item slot rendering and feedback: proportions, count styling, no grab sound
findings.evidence: Icons are 128x128 renders drawn into rect.Grow(-Size.X*0.14), i.e. 72% of the slot. The stack count font is 27% of the slot size (~16px on the 58px hotbar, ~13.5px in the 50px grid), drawn at (0.14*Size, 0.9*Size) in UiTheme.Text. The hotbar badge is 11px in Muted at (4,13). Slot clicks play no sound; hover only lightens the background.
findings.terraria_reference: Slots are 52px at 100%. The item sprite is centred at native size, scaled down only when larger than ~32px (~60% of the slot). The stack number is bottom-left in white with a black outline (FontItemStack); hotbar numbers are top-left in white. Moving items plays the 'Grab' sound. Favourited items get a gold slot.
findings.fix:
In ItemSlotView._Draw:
- Icon rect = Size*0.62, centred.
- Import the 128px icons with mipmaps and draw with TextureFilter LinearWithMipmaps to avoid shimmer at 50-58px.
- Optional: a 1px dark outline canvas_item shader (sample alpha at ±1 texel) for Terraria-like sprite readability.
- Count: white, 4px black outline, size max(12, Size*0.26), at (Size*0.12, Size-6).
- Badge: white at alpha 0.9, 12px.
In the InventoryScreen.Slot click handler call Audio.Sfx.Play("grab") (add grab_1.wav/grab_2.wav to assets/audio/sfx). Draw a gold slot when ItemStack.Favorite is set.

findings.title: Menus close to Terraria's flow but missing logo, hover-scale, themed widgets
findings.evidence:
Good already: a parallax day/night backdrop, borderless text buttons going white -> gold (1,0.86,0.3) on hover with ui_hover/ui_click sounds, and a version label bottom-left. Gaps:
- The title is a text Label '3D Terraria' at 72px.
- Big buttons don't scale on hover.
- Character and world rows use the dark slate Panel(0.95) with framed 'Play'/'Delete' buttons.
- Settings uses unthemed Godot TabContainer, CheckButton, HSlider and OptionButton.
- PauseMenu is a full dim (0.02,0.03,0.06,0.6) with big buttons.
findings.terraria_reference: A logo sprite that slowly rotates, scales and tints with the menu's day/night. Menu items grow (~0.8 -> 1.0 scale) and turn yellow on hover, with a tick sound. Character and world select are blue translucent panels with per-row panels and small icon buttons (play, favourite, delete). In game, Esc opens the inventory with a 'Settings' text button bottom-right rather than a separate pause screen.
findings.fix: MenuKit.Big: on Resized set PivotOffset = Size/2; on MouseEntered tween Scale to 1.08 over 0.08 s, and back on MouseExited. Replace the title Label with a TextureRect logo (assets/ui/logo.png) whose _Process sets Rotation = 0.03f*Mathf.Sin(t*0.6f) and Scale = Vector2.One*(1+0.02f*Mathf.Sin(t)). Character/World rows: panels in Color8(63,82,151,178), hover Color8(73,94,171,200), with 32px icon buttons for play and delete. The theme-coverage fix handles the Settings widgets. Optionally turn PauseMenu into Terraria style: Esc opens the inventory with 'Settings' and 'Save & Exit' text buttons bottom-right, keeping auto-pause.

findings.title: Minimap/map framing and info-accessory readouts are bare; info text overlaps the F3 overlay
findings.evidence: The minimap is a 210px square in the generic panel frame (3px margins) at TopRight (-226,70), with no zoom buttons. Markers are coloured circles and an arrow; labels use ThemeDB.FallbackFont at 13px. The full map has no frame, only a title and a help Label. Info-accessory text (depth/position/time) is a plain Label at (16,64), overlapping the F3 PerfOverlay label at (16,60).
findings.terraria_reference: The minimap sits under the hearts with a decorative frame, zoom +/- and a mode button. NPCs and the player appear as head sprites; the fullscreen map has a frame and names on hover. Info accessories show as icon + text rows stacked on the right under the minimap, each toggleable with an eye in the inventory.
findings.fix:
Minimap: a NinePatchRect frame (assets/ui/minimap_frame.png, 9-slice margins 8) plus two 18px +/- Buttons that change MapView.Zoom (clamp 0.5-6).

MapMarker: add a Texture2D? Icon and DrawTextureRect it when set (NPC heads; player head from a CharacterPreview snapshot). Use GetThemeDefaultFont() instead of ThemeDB.FallbackFont.

Info readouts: move to a VBox anchored TopRight under the minimap (y = 70+210+8). Each row is a 16px icon (depth meter, compass, watch) plus 14px outlined text. This also clears the F3 overlay.

summary: The basic feedback loops are in place: per-material dig and break sounds, dust on block hits and breaks, a crack overlay on the cursor, a red NPC hurt flash with knockback and a brief stun, floating damage numbers, player i-frame blinking with a hurt flinch, material footsteps, torch flicker, a positional SFX pool and a boss > event > biome > layer music director with 31 tracks. What is missing is most of Terraria's "juice", and a few wiring bugs. Every creature uses one generic hit sound, even though EnemyDef.HitSound/DeathSound and hit_squish.wav exist unused. Hits make no blood or gel dust, and deaths leave only a white unshaded sphere puff with no gore. Chopping trees and hitting pots or other objects gives no per-hit sound, particles or progress, and trees just vanish. Pickaxe swing animations restart mid-arc every use. Stone and ores take about 1.7-2x as many hits as in Terraria. Cracks show only on the block under the cursor. Screen shake fires only on explosions. Fall and debuff damage give no hurt sound or number, and first-person play has no hurt indicator. Water entry, projectile impacts, fishing bites and hotbar switches are silent, and the Ambient bus plays nothing. Item pickups spam a corner toast list instead of Terraria's merged popup above the head, and there is no smart cursor, auto-select or quick-heal. Movement tuning is snappier than Terraria and the jump is about half as high relative to the body, which suits 3D, but the knockback on both players and NPCs is weak.

findings.title: Enemy hit/death sounds are generic; per-creature sound fields and hit_squish asset unused; DoT ticks play hit sounds
findings.evidence: SoundEvents.cs:42 `Sfx.PlayAt("hit", ToGodot(e.Position), e.Crit ? 2f : 0f);` for every creature (45 ms throttle at :40). Death at :46 is hardcoded: gel tag→slime_death, skeleton/cursed_skull/dungeon_guardian→hit_bone, else npc_death. EnemyDef.HitSound/DeathSound (EnemyDef.cs:206-207) have zero references in src/ or game/ and no data file sets them. hit_squish_1..3.wav have 0 code references. DamageEvent has no npc or periodic flag, so the damage-over-time tick at NpcSystem.cs:161 (every 60 ticks while burning or poisoned) plays the same 'hit' SFX.
findings.terraria_reference: Every NPC has NPC.HitSound and NPC.DeathSound: NPCHit1 flesh, NPCHit2 bone, NPCHit4 metal, NPCHit1 plus gel squish for slimes; NPCDeath1/2/... on kill. Debuff damage-over-time plays no hit sound.
findings.fix: Core: extend DamageEvent with `long? NpcId` and `bool Periodic` (set Periodic=true at NpcSystem.cs:161). ContentLoader/DerivedContent: default HitSound/DeathSound from tags/model when unset (gel→hit_squish/slime_death, skeleton/bone→hit_bone, construct/metal→dig_metal, default→hit/npc_death). SoundEvents: look up the npc by id and play `npc.Def.HitSound ?? "hit"` at its position, skip when Periodic, and play the death sound from `Def.DeathSound` instead of the hardcoded switch.

findings.title: No hit dust/blood on enemies; death is a white unshaded sphere puff with no gore
findings.evidence: Damaged only spawns a number (CombatEffects.cs:16). Killed calls `Puff(center, Color.FromHtml(npc.Def.Tint), ...)` (:17): 18 SphereMesh particles with an Unshaded material (:94). Tint defaults to "#ffffff" (EnemyDef.cs:183) and only 79 `tint` entries exist across data/enemies, so most deaths make a white puff, full-bright even in dark caves. Non-human corpses just shrink over ShrinkTime=0.3 s; humans play a death clip and sink after 1.7 s (NpcRenderer.Motion.cs:26).
findings.terraria_reference: Each hit spawns 3-10 dust of the NPC's type (blood for flesh, gel colored like the slime, bone or metal sparks). Death bursts 20-40 dust plus 2-4 gore pieces (head/arm/leg) that tumble, bounce and fade.
findings.fix: Add `HitDust` ("blood"|"gel"|"bone"|"spark"|"ichor") and optional `DustColor` to EnemyDef, defaulted from tags. In CombatEffects add pooled `HitBurst(DamageEvent)` (4 + dmg/10 chips, capped at 12) and on Killed a 25-chip burst plus 2-4 larger box 'gore' chunks tinted by DustColor with gravity -12 and fading. Replace the Unshaded sphere material with the voxel-lit sprite_lit shader, or set a voxel_light instance param from LightProbe.SampleSmooth, so puffs do not glow in caves. Pool the emitters as BlockEffects does instead of new CpuParticles3D per puff (:76).

findings.title: Chopping trees and hitting objects is silent and invisible; trees vanish instantly; all objects break with 'break_wood'
findings.evidence: HitObject does `obj.HitPoints -= Math.Max(1, power / 40)` and returns Damaged without raising any event (WorldEditor.Objects.cs:64-65). UseOutcome.HitObject has no case in SoundEvents.OnUsed (:99-127), and pickaxes/axes carry Melee, but the outcome is not rewritten to Swung (ItemUseSystem.cs:157), so there is no whoosh either. ObjectBroken always plays `break_wood` (SoundEvents.cs:30), even for pots, glass and stone furniture. BlockEffects subscribes only to Struck and BlockPlaced, so objects make no chips. The cursor draws a Neutral box with no progress for objects (TargetHighlight.cs:64-65). Oak tree hitPoints 6 with a copper axe (axePower 35 → 1 per hit, useTime 21) means 6 silent hits, then the tree disappears.
findings.terraria_reference: Each axe hit plays Dig, spawns wood dust and shakes the tree. On fell, the trunk breaks from the hit point up with leaf and wood gore. Pots shatter with their own sound and gore, and every object type has its own kill sound and dust.
findings.fix: Core: add `event Action<TileObjectInstance, ObjectHitResult>? ObjectHit` raised in HitObject for Damaged and Broken. Add `Sound` (default "wood") and `DustColor` to TileObjectDef. SoundEvents: on ObjectHit play `dig_{def.Sound}`, and on ObjectBroken play `break_{def.Sound}`. BlockEffects: burst chips from the object bounds (5 per hit, 25 on break, plus green leaf chips for trees). TileObjectRenderer: ±3° wobble tween for 0.15 s on hit, and a topple animation for trees (rotate 90° about the base over 0.8 s, then a puff) before release. TargetHighlight: pass `1 - obj.HitPoints/obj.Def.HitPoints` to `_mesh.Faces` so objects get the crack overlay.

findings.title: Pickaxe and axe swing animations restart mid-arc on every use (useTime < useAnimation)
findings.evidence: Each use sets `p.UseCooldown = useTime; p.UseAnimation = item.UseAnimation;` (ItemUseSystem.cs:161-162). The avatar replays the action whenever `use > _lastUse` (PlayerAvatar.Motion.cs:46), and the ViewModel phase `t = 1 - UseAnimation/item.UseAnimation` snaps back (ViewModel.cs:51). Copper pickaxe useTime 15 / useAnimation 21, iron 13/19, gold 11/17, copper axe 21/27, so the arc restarts at 71% / 68% / 65% / 78%, a visible stutter while holding the button. MeleeSystem.Start also discards the in-flight swing (:46).
findings.terraria_reference: A swing (itemAnimation) always plays to the end. Tile hits happen on the itemTime cadence inside it, and the next swing starts only when itemAnimation reaches 0, so holding a pickaxe reads as a smooth continuous chop.
findings.fix: In ItemUseSystem.Use, only restart the animation when the previous one has finished: `if (p.UseAnimation <= 0) p.UseAnimation = item.UseAnimation;`. For tools, let the dig repeat on UseCooldown inside the swing. Alternatively raise the Used event with a 'newSwing' flag and have PlayerAvatar and ViewModel start a new action only on it. In ViewModel, derive the phase from a continuous accumulator that loops, not from the countdown.

findings.title: Mining stone and ores takes about 1.7-2x the hits of Terraria (hardness scales block HP)
findings.evidence: Health = 100f * block.Hardness, and damage per hit = item.PickPower (`editor.Mine(cells, item.PickPower, item.PickPower, tick)`). Dirt 0.8 → 80 HP, stone 1.5 → 150, copper ore 1.6 → 160, iron ore 1.8 → 180, hellstone 3.0 → 300. Copper Pickaxe (35 power, useTime 15): dirt 3 hits (0.50 s), stone 5 hits (1.00 s), iron ore 6 hits (1.25 s). Gold (55, useTime 11): stone 3 hits.
