Partial damage is forgotten after ForgetAfterTicks = 360 (6 s) with no visual decay.
findings.terraria_reference: Every tile has 100 HP and damage per hit equals pick power. Soft tiles (dirt, sand, clay, mud, snow, ash, silt, slush) take double. Only special tiles take a fraction: ebonstone, crimstone, pearlstone, hellstone and dungeon bricks ½, cobalt/palladium ½, mythril/orichalcum ⅓, adamantite/titanium ¼, chlorophyte ⅕. A Copper Pickaxe breaks dirt in 2 hits and stone or ores in 3 (about 0.5 s), which gives Terraria its brisk mining.
findings.fix: Replace hardness-as-HP with a Terraria-style model: Health = 100 for every block, plus a BlockDef `pickDamageScale` (default 1; 2 for soil/sand/snow tags; 0.5/0.33/0.25/0.2 for the special tiers). In WorldEditor.Mine, multiply damage by the scale. Keep `hardness` only for sound and particle intensity. Migrate data/blocks/*.json (a ~30-line data change) and add a unit test that asserts copper pick on stone takes 3 hits.

findings.title: Crack overlay only on the block under the cursor; damaged blocks elsewhere show nothing
findings.evidence: TargetHighlight returns early unless there is a target within reach (:52). Progress is the max over the brush cells (:92), sent as one material uniform `progress` (SelectionMesh.cs:90-91), and the shader draws with depth_test_disabled on the cursor box. BlockDamageTracker.Active(tick) exists (MiningRules.cs:78-79) but nothing in game/ reads it. Look away from a half-mined block and its cracks disappear, even though damage persists for 6 s.
findings.terraria_reference: Every damaged tile draws a crack overlay in 3-4 stages by damage %, whether or not the cursor is on it. Cracks go away when the tile's hit counter decays.
findings.fix: Add game/Rendering/BlockCracks.cs: each frame take up to 64 entries from `Editor.Damage.Active(tick)`, draw a MultiMesh of slightly inflated cubes (1.01 × cell) with per-instance custom data = damage/health, and use a crack shader derived from selection.gdshader with depth test enabled, stepped into 4 stages like Terraria. Keep the cursor's fill and outline, but stop drawing cracks on it so they are not doubled.

findings.title: Player hurt feedback: fall and debuff damage are silent, first person has no hurt cue, knockback sets off the jump sound, knockback is weak
findings.evidence: Present: player_hurt sound (SoundEvents.cs:37), red number, i-frames PlayerHitImmunity = 40 ticks (NpcSystem.cs:27), blink `(immune / 4) % 2` (PlayerAvatar.cs:47), flinch (PlayerAvatar.Motion.cs:49-51), control loss 0.25 s with accel × 0.15 (PlayerController.cs:152-156, 186). Missing: the FallDamaged event (PlayerController.cs:46, 269) has no subscriber, and DoT uses Vitals.DamageDirect (GameWorld.cs:282) without ReportPlayerDamage, so neither makes a sound or number. In first person the avatar is hidden (PlayerAvatar.cs:47), so there is no hurt visual at all. Contact knock is `away*(2.5 + kb*0.6) + (0, 4.5, 0)` (NpcSystem.cs:265), about 6.1 m/s ≈ 3.4 body-heights/s. Lava sets v.Y = 7 (LiquidEffects.cs:143). Both exceed the `v.Y > 3f` jump-sound check (PlayerController.Sound.cs:29), so getting hit plays the jump sound.
findings.terraria_reference: Player.Hurt sets velocity.X = 4.5 px/tick × dir (≈16.9 tiles/s ≈ 6.4 body heights/s) and velocity.Y = -3.5 (≈13 tiles/s up), plays the hurt sound, pops a red number (255,80,90) for every damage source including falls, and grants 40 i-frames while the sprite flickers. Terraria has no jump sound.
findings.fix: 1) Fire the jump sound from UpdateJump when a jump actually starts (a `Jumped` event next to AirJumped) instead of inferring it from velocity. 2) Route fall damage through Core: after `DamageDirect`, call `_runtime.Game.Npcs.ReportPlayerDamage(Entity, damage, Vector3.Zero)`. Do the same for DoT in GameWorld.cs:282, throttled to one number per second. 3) Add game/UI/HurtOverlay.cs, a full-rect ColorRect with a radial red vignette shader: alpha 0.35 → 0 over 0.35 s on local PlayerHurt, plus `CameraShake.Kick(0.12 + 0.4*dmg/MaxLife)`. 4) Scale the contact knock toward Terraria: horizontal 4 + kb*0.6, vertical 5.5.

findings.title: Screen shake only on explosions; nothing for boss spawn/defeat, heavy hits or hard landings; no hitstop
findings.evidence: The only CameraShake.Kick call site is CombatEffects.cs:35 (`Mathf.Clamp(radius * 0.35f, 0.2f, 1f)`). BossSpawned and BossDefeated only play a sound (SoundEvents.cs:49-50). Shake is translation only via HOffset/VOffset, amplitude `trauma² * 0.35` m, decaying 1.2/s (CameraShake.cs:20-23). Engine.TimeScale appears only in a debug command (EngineCommands.cs:77), so there is no hitstop or freeze-frame anywhere.
findings.terraria_reference: Terraria 1.4 punches the camera (PunchCameraModifier) at heavy boss moments, for example the Deerclops roar, Queen Slime slams and Moon Lord, gated by the Screen Shake option. Terraria has no hitstop; its punch comes from snappy knockback plus sound.
findings.fix: Add `CameraShake.Punch(Vector3 dir, float strength, float seconds)` with a small roll component (Camera.Rotation.Z ±1.5°). Kick 0.45 on BossSpawned, 0.7 on BossDefeated, 0.1-0.35 on local PlayerHurt scaled by damage fraction, and 0.15 on landings with airVelocityY < -14 m/s. Optional and cheap instead of global hitstop: on crits and kills, freeze that NPC's view.Shown for 3 frames and scale-punch it 1.15 → 1.0 over 0.1 s in NpcRenderer, and flash a hit-marker X on Hud.Crosshair (Hud.cs:322-343) for 0.12 s on local damage events.

findings.title: Many gameplay events have no sound; Ambient bus unused; SFX pool drops sounds silently
findings.evidence: There are 70 SFX ids under assets/audio/sfx. Unused: fish_bite (0 refs, even though bobber Biting is simulated at ProjectileSystem.Special.cs:189) and hit_squish (0 refs). No sound for: entering or leaving water (`_swimming = _liquid != null` flips silently, PlayerController.cs:134), projectile impacts (Removed just QueueFrees, ProjectileRenderer.cs:31), hotbar switches (InteractionController.cs:172-182), or the tool whoosh when a pickaxe connects (only UseOutcome.Swung plays 'swing', SoundEvents.cs:101-103). Too-hard uses dig_* at -8 dB instead of a tink (:84-85). Placing is one generic 'place' for every material (:92). ItemDef.SoundSet is never read. AudioBuses.Ambient (Sfx.cs:105) has no players: no wind, birds, crickets, cave drips or lava bubbling. The pool is 12 2D plus 12 3D players, and `Free()` returns null when all are busy, so the sound is simply dropped with no voice stealing (Sfx.cs:40-41, 63-68).
findings.terraria_reference: Item1 swing on every tool or weapon use, including when a tile is hit. Dig for each tile hit and placement. Tink (SoundID 21) when the pick is too weak. Splash plus dust on water entry and exit. A fishing-bite splash. MenuTick on hotbar change. Grab on pickup. Projectile tile-hit sounds (Dig or arrow thunk). 1.4 ambience: birds by day, crickets and owls at night, wind, waterfalls, lava.
findings.fix: SoundEvents: play 'swing' at -6 dB for any tool use (hook ItemUse.Used whenever info.IsTool); use `dig_{material}` pitched +10% for placement; add tink.wav for TooHard. PlayerController.Sound: play splash on _swimming edge transitions (volume by |v.Y|). Core ProjectileSystem: add `event Action<Projectile, Vector3, ushort block>? HitTerrain`, then play dig_{material} at -6 dB with a 4-chip BlockEffects burst. ProjectileRenderer: play fish_bite when p.Biting flips true. Hotbar: Sfx.Play("ui_hover", -10). Sfx: add per-id max voices plus oldest-voice stealing, and raise the pool to 24. Add game/Audio/AmbienceDirector.cs: two looping players on the Ambient bus crossfaded by biome, time and layer (surface_day, surface_night, cave, lava, ocean).

findings.title: Damage numbers work but lack pop, heal/mana numbers and Terraria colors; NPC health is a text label, not a bar
findings.evidence: Label3D with FontSize 56 (72 on crits) and PixelSize 0.005. Colors: hostile (1, 0.9, 0.45), crit (1, 0.6, 0.15), player (1, 0.3, 0.3). The tween rises 1.1 m over 0.9 s (cubic out) and starts fading after 0.3 s (:45-51), with no scale pop. There are no heal or mana numbers: Vitals.Heal (Vitals.cs:60) raises no event. NPC health is shown as the text `$"{npc.Life}/{npc.MaxLife}"` in a red Label3D above the head (NpcRenderer.cs:148).
findings.terraria_reference: CombatText pops in with a quick scale-up, then drifts up and slows while fading. Colors: DamagedHostile (255,160,80), crit (255,100,30) larger, DamagedFriendly (255,80,90), HealLife green (100,255,100), HealMana blue (100,100,255). Damaged NPCs show a small green→yellow→red health bar beneath them, not numbers.
findings.fix: CombatEffects.Number: set label.Scale = 1.6 and tween it to 1.0 in 0.12 s (Back ease), switch to the Terraria colors, and add a slight random x drift. Add `event Action<int>? Healed` / `ManaRestored` to Core Vitals (or surface them from GameWorld) and show green and blue numbers above the local player. Replace the NPC Label3D with a billboarded QuadMesh bar (a shader with a fill uniform and a color ramp) placed under the creature, shown for 3 s after damage.

findings.title: Item pickup popups are a corner toast list, not Terraria's merged popup above the player
findings.evidence: Each pickup adds a new Label to the right-centre VBox: `Toast($"+{stack.Count} {stack.Item!.DisplayName}", UiTheme.Rarity(...))`, 2.2 s hold and 0.6 s fade, capped at 6 by deleting the oldest (Hud.cs:163, 269-279). Mining a vein floods it with duplicates. Sound is right: 'coins' for the coin tag, else 'pickup'. Magnet range is 3.2 m, pickup 1.0 m, and items lerp toward the player at 9 m/s (DroppedItems.cs:29-30, 83).
findings.terraria_reference: PopupText floats over the player's head in rarity color, e.g. "Dirt Block (37)". Repeated pickups of the same item within a few seconds merge into one popup, bump the count and re-pop. Coins aggregate into one value shown in coin colors. Grab sound on pickup.
findings.fix: Add game/UI/PickupPopups.cs, a CanvasLayer that projects a point 2.1 m above the player and stacks labels upward. Keep a Dictionary<itemId, Popup>; within 2 s, add to the count, restart the fade and play a 1.25 → 1.0 scale pop. Sum all coin pickups into one value formatted as platinum/gold/silver/copper with coin colors. Route Hud's ItemPickedUp there and keep toasts for messages only.

findings.title: No jump, land or run dust and no water splash particles
findings.evidence: The land and jump logic only plays audio (PlayerController.Sound.cs:27-29). The only body particles are the double-jump cloud puff and rocket-boot flames (PlayerAvatar.Gear.cs:10, 43). _swimming toggles with no visual (PlayerController.cs:134). Footsteps are sound-only.
findings.terraria_reference: Water and lava entry or exit throws splash dust in the liquid's color. Speed boots and dashes kick up dust from the tile underfoot, and double jumps puff clouds.
findings.fix: Add game/Player/PlayerDust.cs with a pooled CpuParticles3D reusing BlockEffects' chip setup. Colors come from `session.Content.Blocks[id].Color` of the cell under the feet (reuse StepSound's lookup). Trigger 8 chips on landings with airVelocityY < -8, 2 chips per footstep while sprinting, 6 chips on dash, and a 16-particle ring in `_liquid.Color` whenever _swimming flips.

findings.title: No smart cursor, auto-select or quick heal/mana/buff; only 'Smart dig' when looking down
findings.evidence: SmartDig is the only assist: with a Mine tool and aim `dir.Y <= -0.8`, it targets the block under the feet (InteractionController.cs:133-143). input.json has no smart_cursor, auto_select, quick_heal, quick_mana or quick_buff actions.
findings.terraria_reference: Ctrl toggles Smart Cursor: a pickaxe auto-targets the nearest minable tile along the cursor line within range, an axe targets the nearest tree, torches go on the nearest valid wall, and blocks and platforms fill sensibly. Holding Shift (Auto Select) swaps to the right tool for what is under the cursor (pickaxe, axe, torch in the dark, bucket at liquid). H quick-heals with the best potion, J quick-mana, B quick-buff. These are core to Terraria's mining flow.
findings.fix: Add actions smart_cursor (toggle), auto_select (hold), quick_heal (H), quick_mana (J) and quick_buff (B). Core Targeting: `SmartTarget(world, eye, aim, reachMeters, ItemUseInfo)`, which walks the ray up to reach and, for Mine, picks the nearest mineable cell within a 20° cone and 1 block of the ray; for Chop, the nearest axe-breakable object. InteractionController: while auto_select is held, temporarily select the hotbar slot whose ItemUseInfo matches the target (restore on release). Core ItemUseSystem: `QuickUse(PlayerEntity, Func<ItemDef,bool>)` that consumes the best matching backpack potion, respecting the healing_cooldown buff.

findings.title: Cursor reach ignores the Reach stat bonus (Builder), so placeable targets show as out of range
findings.evidence: Cursor: `float reach = (held.IsEmpty ? 10 : held.Item!.Reach) * CellSize;` (InteractionController.cs:101). Use: `(item.Reach + p.State.Effects.Stats.Bonus(StatIds.Reach)) * Units.CellSize` (ItemUseSystem.cs:94). The Builder buff adds reach +2 (alchemy.json:22). In that extra 1 m, InReach is false, so the ghost, cracks and crosshair go dim and object interaction is refused, even though mining and placing succeed. Default reach is 10 cells = 5 m from the eye (ItemDef.cs:52), roughly Terraria's 5-6 tiles for 1 m grid blocks. Builder's 'placement speed' is not implemented; only reach is.
findings.terraria_reference: tileRangeX 5 / tileRangeY 4 tiles from the player's hitbox edges, plus the item's tileBoost; Builder Potion adds +1 range and +25% placement speed. The cursor and the use always agree.
findings.fix: Add a single Core helper `ItemUseSystem.ReachMeters(PlayerEntity p, ItemDef item)` and call it from both InteractionController.UpdateTarget and Use. Add a `placeSpeed` stat applied to useTime for PlaceBlock/PlaceObject, and give the builder buff placeSpeed 0.25.

findings.title: Enemy hit flash and knockback exist, but the vertical 'pop' is tiny and there is no squash on hit
findings.evidence: On hit: `npc.HurtFlash = 8` (133 ms), then red tint `new Color(2.2f, 0.7f, 0.7f)` (NpcRenderer.cs:142), and humanoids play Hurt() (Motion.cs:157). Melee immunity is 10 ticks. The push is `away * kb * 2.0 + (0, kb * 0.4, 0)` and replaces horizontal velocity, with stun 6 + 2*kb ticks. At kb 5 that is 10 m/s sideways but only 2 m/s up, a ~9 cm hop at Brain.Gravity 22. Ground drag 0.88 per tick carries it about 1.4 m. Bosses and kb < 0.3 only add velocity.
findings.terraria_reference: Knockback throws grounded enemies visibly up and back in an arc (vertical roughly proportional to knockback), so a Copper Broadsword (kb 5) sends a zombie hopping 2-3 tiles. Crits multiply knockback by 1.4.
findings.fix: NpcSystem.Knock: set the vertical to `MathF.Max(2.5f, knockback * 1.1f)` for grounded non-bosses and apply ground drag only after landing. NpcRenderer: on HurtFlash rising, set view.Squash = 0.8 (squashable) or apply a 1.12 → 1.0 scale punch over 0.1 s to every creature. Fade the flash out rather than on/off (lerp the tint by HurtFlash/8).

findings.title: Block hit/break dust present but single-colored and not voxel-lit
findings.evidence: Hit: 7 chips at speed 1.8 living 0.5 s. Break: 22 chips at 3.2 living 0.9 s. Too-hard: 3 chips. Place: 6 chips (:31, :49). All chips are one color, `Color.FromHtml(def.Color).Darkened(0.1f)`, 0.07 m boxes with a plain lit StandardMaterial3D (:23-24). Unlike dropped items, which set a voxel_light instance param from LightProbe (DroppedItemRenderer.cs:54), chips ignore the voxel lighting that terrain uses, so they will not match cave darkness or torchlight.
findings.terraria_reference: Each tile type has its own dust type with 2-3 color variations (grass green plus dirt brown, ore flecks, glass sparkle, sand drifting down). About 3-5 dust per hit and 10+ on break, all lit by tile lighting.
findings.fix: Give BlockEffects a sprite_lit-style shader, or set the chip MaterialOverride per burst with the voxel light sampled at the burst point. Randomize per-particle color with a Gradient/ColorRamp between def.Color lightened 0.15 and darkened 0.3. Add a BlockDef `dust` style: "grass" mixes green top chips, "ore" adds bright flecks of the ore color, "glass" makes sparkly chips with low gravity, "sand"/"snow" makes slow-falling, non-bouncing chips. On break, add 2-3 larger 0.14 m chunks.

findings.title: Movement and jump tuning: snappier than Terraria, jump only about half as high relative to the body
findings.evidence: walkSpeed 5, sprint ×1.35 (6.75 m/s), groundAcceleration 40, groundFriction 30, airAcceleration 22, gravity 32, jumpSpeed 9.2, jumpHoldGravity 0.45 for jumpHoldTime 0.28 s, coyote and buffer 0.12 s, stepHeight 0.55. Derived: top speed in 0.125 s, stop in 0.17 s, full-hold jump apex ≈ 2.43 m (1.35 × the 1.8 m body), tap ≈ 1.32 m, about 0.44 s to apex. Auto-step clears one 0.5 m cell but not a 1 m grid block.
findings.terraria_reference: maxRunSpeed 3 px/tick (≈11.25 tiles/s ≈ 4.3 body heights/s), runAcceleration 0.08 (≈0.6 s to top speed), runSlowdown 0.2 (≈0.25 s stop). Jump: jumpSpeed 5.01 held for 15 ticks, gravity 0.4, for about 6 tiles (≈2.3 body heights) and about 0.45 s to apex. Auto-steps up a full 1-tile ledge. Full air control.
findings.fix: Keep the snappy acceleration, which suits 3D aiming, but raise the jump toward Terraria's proportions: jumpSpeed 10.5 and jumpHoldTime 0.30 give ≈3.1 m (1.7 bodies) and clear a 2-block wall with margin. Add Terraria's turnaround feel: when `wish · horizontal < 0`, use accel × 1.5. Consider stepHeight 1.05 so the player walks up a single 1 m grid block like Terraria's 1-tile auto-step, gated on no ceiling. Put the result in movement.json and a regression test on apex height.

findings.title: Music director is solid, with content gaps (rain, town, underground-biome and night variants, boss-defeat stinger)
findings.evidence: Priority: nearest living boss > active event > blood moon > biome by priority (night variant via `_day`→`_night`) > layer fallback. 2.0 s crossfade (:16), re-evaluated every 0.75 s (:73). 31 tracks, and every `music` reference in data resolves, with 14 boss themes collapsed into boss_1/boss_2/boss_3/boss_queen/boss_lunar through Aliases (:18-26). Only forest has a night variant. Underground falls back to underground/cavern except underground_desert. No rain, town or space-specific tracks, and nothing marks the moment a boss is defeated beyond an SFX.
findings.terraria_reference: Separate Day/Night overworld themes, Rain, Windy Day, Town Day/Night (1.4.4), Space, underground variants (Underground Corruption, Crimson, Hallow, Snow, Jungle, Desert), Mushroom, and per-boss themes. Music fades out when a boss dies.
findings.fix: Move Aliases into data/config/music.json. Add states to Choose(): 'rain' when session weather is raining on the surface, 'town_day'/'town_night' when ≥3 housed residents are within 40 m, and `underground_{biomeId}` resolved before the layer fallback (then Resolve falls back to aliases). On BossDefeated, fade to -30 dB for 2 s before resuming. Add the matching .ogg tracks to assets/audio/music.

findings.title: Autoswing, hold-to-mine, placement speed and footsteps work
findings.evidence: `repeats = item.AutoReuse || info.IsTool || Place* || Melee || Thrust` (ItemUseSystem.cs:89), and the button is polled every physics tick (InteractionController.cs:61-66). Derived block items use useTime 12 with autoReuse; objects use 15. Footsteps fire every 1.6 m at -4 dB with ±0.1 pitch and pick grass/sand/snow/wood/stone by BlockDef.Sound.
findings.terraria_reference: 1.4.4 autoswings all melee weapons; tools and blocks auto-reuse (blocks useTime 10 / useAnimation 15). Terraria has no footstep sounds, so these are a 3D bonus.
findings.fix: No change needed. Optionally use useTime 10 for blocks to match Terraria's placement rate exactly.

findings.title: Torch and fire flicker are convincing
findings.evidence: Fire lights layer three sines (17.3, 7.1 and 23.9 Hz) with a per-source seed. The held-torch light adds a gutter term. Shader flames billboard, the held torch has embers, and lava gets drifting embers plus a slow heat-light pulse.
findings.terraria_reference: Torches flicker and emit occasional sparks; lava glows and bubbles.
findings.fix: No change needed. Optionally emit a rare spark CpuParticle from placed torches within 10 m to match Terraria's torch dust.

summary: The Blender pipeline (tools/blender/build_all.py + bgen/*) is solid. The recent boss rebuilds (King Slime 7,030 tris, Eye of Cthulhu 10,558, Brain 10,320, Twins ~9,276, Skeletron 7,794, Deerclops 17,894) read clearly as their Terraria counterparts. Almost everything else is one generic primitive mesh per archetype, recoloured through assets.json. All 42 swords are the same 88-triangle, 5-vertex blade (Zenith and Terra Blade included). There are 26 pickaxes at 80 tris, 21 hammers that are a 36-tri box on a stick, 25 identical gem staffs, and all 34 helmets are the same dome (the Wizard Hat is a near-black metal dome). Creatures fall into three fidelity tiers: humans average 54,138 tris, bosses 5-18k, and common enemies 36-800 tris. Many enemies also borrow the wrong archetype: the wolf and Headless Horseman are horned unicorns, the Black Recluse is a crab, the Mimic is a gift box, the Flying Snake is a vulture, and the Bone Serpent is the Eater of Worlds head tinted bone. Item icons are thin Cycles renders with no outline: weapons cover only 1.7-7.7% of the 128px frame, gun icons render edge-on as black sticks, and metal colours go muddy because the tint is multiplied onto a grey iron texture (copper, palladium and hellstone all come out brown). Worn armour is never drawn on the player, and the held item and wings ignore voxel light. Suggested order: fix icon framing, outlines and gun orientation, and correct metal colours (cheap, and every inventory slot benefits). Then reuse the boss-quality helpers (detail.organic, _eyeball, _slime_body) for the most-seen enemies. Next add silhouette variety to weapons and tools, fix the wrong-archetype creatures, and rebuild the primitive event bosses. Visible armour is the largest single Terraria-feel gap.

findings.title: Every weapon/tool class is one mesh recoloured; iconic uniques share the generic silhouette
findings.evidence: Measured from GLBs. sword n=42, all exactly 88 tris (1 distinct mesh). pickaxe n=26 at 80 tris; axe n=26 at 60; hammer n=21 at 36 tris (items.py:55 is one mb.box head on a 7-sided haft); staff n=25 at 104; bow n=23 at 144; helmet n=34 at 122; chest_armor n=32 at 156; greaves n=32 at 92; bar n=23 at 24 tris. The blade is always a 5-point polygon `[(-w/2,0.07),(w/2,0.07),(w/2,L*0.85),(0,L),(-w/2,L*0.85)]` with a box guard, sphere pommel and a silver fuller `#e8ecf0` (items.py:22-25). Zenith, Terra Blade, Night's Edge, Meowmere, Star Wrath, Muramasa, Influx Waver and Breaker Blade differ only in `metal`/`guard`/`length`/`width`/`glow` params. The zenith, terra_blade, nights_edge and muramasa icons are the same cross-hilt longsword in cyan, green, purple and blue.
findings.terraria_reference: Every Terraria tool tier has its own sprite silhouette: copper's stubby pick, gold's ornate head, Nightmare/Deathbringer's spiky evil heads, Molten's flaming pick. Swords are instantly recognisable by shape: Terra Blade's jagged green blade, Night's Edge's hooked purple blade, Muramasa's thin katana, Meowmere's cat hilt, Zenith's layered blade.
findings.fix: (1) Turn items.sword into a profile-driven generator. Add params `profile` (named list in a new bgen/blade_profiles.py: straight, leaf, broad, katana, curved, serrated, hooked, jagged, cleaver), `guard` style (bar, crescent, winged, disc, none), `pommel` (ball, gem, ring), `edge` colour, `gem`, `serration`, and `curve` via bmesh bend of the extruded polygon. Replace the fixed fuller with `fuller` true/false. (2) Give the {metal}_* patterns (assets.json:493-560) a per-metal style table in build_all.plan: copper/tin simple, iron/lead straight, silver/tungsten fuller, gold/platinum ornate guard, demonite/crimtane spiky evil profile. Tools get tier head shapes by adding `head` variants to pickaxe/axe/hammer (items.py:36-55): a tapered bevelled hammer head (lathe/extrude, not a box) and a pick head from an extruded curved polygon rather than a 6-segment tube. (3) Add bgen/weapons_unique.py with bespoke generators for the ~15 highest-visibility uniques: Zenith, Terra Blade, Night's Edge, True Night's Edge, Excalibur, True Excalibur, Muramasa, Meowmere, Star Wrath, Influx Waver, Starfury, Enchanted Sword, Breaker Blade, Lucy the Axe, Death Sickle. Register them in build_all.build (line 139). Target 300-1500 tris per weapon.

findings.title: Item icons are thin, unoutlined Cycles renders; they don't read like Terraria inventory sprites
findings.evidence: Icons are 128x128, ORTHO, 24 Cycles samples with `use_denoising = False`, two suns (3.5/1.2) and a grey world 0.55,0.58,0.62 at strength 0.8. There is no outline pass. Measured average opaque coverage of the frame: spear 1.7%, rod 2.9%, arrow 4.3%, staff 4.6%, pickaxe 5.3%, bow 5.4%, sword 7.7%, hammer 10.1%, axe 11.4%, vs crate 64.9%, tome 50.4%. Swords are 1,298 of 16,384 px. The icon material fixes roughness 0.7 with no metallic, while in-game metal layers are metallic 1.0 (gen_built.py:196), so icons and held models don't match. docs/screenshots/m1_inventory.png shows hairline sword/pickaxe icons next to a chunky wood cube.
findings.terraria_reference: Terraria item sprites are chunky pixel art. They have a 1-2 px dark outline, fill the slot on the diagonal, use saturated, high-contrast colours with a light top-left edge, and stay legible at 32-40 px.
findings.fix: In export.render_icon: (a) for the 'item' view, frame on the rotated diagonal and add an icon-only thickness boost (scale the pivot 1.6x on the axis perpendicular to the blade) so weapons cover 20-30%. (b) Enable denoising and render at 256, then downsample. (c) Add a compositor outline: dilate alpha 2 px, fill with the item's darkened colour (x0.3), composite under the render. (d) Optional pixel mode: render at 48-64 px and nearest-upscale, quantising to ~24 colours. (e) Add a top-left rim light and a Filmic/AgX 'Medium High Contrast' look to push saturation. Keep the 3/4 view for objects. Rebuild with `--only=` per class; build_icons.py block cubes should get the same outline pass for consistency.

findings.title: Gun (and chainsaw) icons render edge-on as black sticks
findings.evidence: The gun side profile is built in the YZ plane: grip box y -0.06..0.02, receiver y 0..0.07, barrel at y=0.045, accent rail y 0.07..0.085, but width only x ±0.03 (gear.py:76-90). 'gun' is in `long_items` (build_all.py:254), so the icon camera looks along +Y (`direction = Vector((0.0, -1.0, 0.05))`, export.py:88) and sees only the 6 cm-wide edge. flintlock_pistol, minishark and megashark icons are dark vertical bars; minishark and megashark icons look identical. All 28 guns are 52-156 tris with 6 distinct meshes. The chainsaw bar is x ±0.015 with teeth on ±Y (gear.py:260-264), so it is invisible side-on as well.
findings.terraria_reference: Minishark, Megashark, Flintlock, Boomstick, Space Gun and Star Cannon are some of the most recognisable Terraria sprites, always drawn in side profile, barrel to the right.
findings.fix: Model guns in XZ like swords: swap the y/x roles in gear.gun (grip toward -X, barrel along +Z, receiver depth along Y), or add a `profile_axis` param with a final `bmesh.ops.rotate` of 90 deg about Z. Give each style a real silhouette via extrude_polygon (stock, trigger guard, magazine, sights; Minishark/Megashark shark-fin top and mouth, Star Cannon star muzzle, Space Gun ray-gun bulb). Apply the same rotation to chainsaw (gear.py:255-264) and drill. Rebuild with `--only=*gun*,minishark,megashark,...`.

findings.title: Wrong-archetype creature models: many enemies borrow an unrelated generator
findings.evidence: `steed` always builds the spiralled glowing crystal horn (beasts.py:93-101, only its colour is a param). So wolf, hellhound, headless_horseman (no rider), wither_beast, drakin and drakomire are horned horses (all 2,116 tris). `crab` (348 tris: 2 claws + 6 legs) is used for black_recluse, wall_creeper, salamander, giant_tortoise, antlion, antlion_charger, anomura_fungus and blood_crawler. The hornet `insect` (254 tris) is used for mothron, eater_of_souls, crimera, derpling, beetle, mushi_ladybug, predictor, moth and lacewing. `jelly` (300 tris) serves granite_elemental, ice_elemental and gastropod. Vulture `bird` serves flying_snake, raven, parrot and etherian_wyvern. `present` (a gift box with a ribbon, 204 tris) serves the Mimic. Via data `model`: eater_of_worlds_head is reused for giant_worm, devourer, digger, bone_serpent and tomb_crawler (tint only); gel for snow_flinx; fish for shark; probe for deadly_sphere, martian_drone and elf_copter; demon_eye for drippler and ichor_sticker.
findings.terraria_reference: The Wolf is a grey wolf, the Headless Horseman a headless rider on a black horse, and the Black Recluse and Wall Creeper eight-legged spiders. The Mimic is a chest with teeth and legs, the Flying Snake a winged serpent, and the Bone Serpent a skull with vertebrae. Eater of Souls is a worm-bodied flying mouth, Crimera a floating crimson face, Snow Flinx a furry snowball critter, the Shark a shark. The elementals are floating rock or ice clusters.
findings.fix:
Add params and generators within the existing modules:
- `steed`: `horn: false`, plus a `head: 'canine'` variant (muzzle, pointed ears, fur tail) for wolf/hellhound.
- Headless horseman: build the rider with the humanoid pipeline; its armature is separate, so export it as a second creature `headless_horseman_rider` drawn attached by the renderer, the way armModel is.
- New fauna.spider (8 jointed legs, cephalothorax, fangs; rig: leg pairs).
- fauna.lizard (salamander).
- fauna.tortoise (domed shell via detail.organic).
- An antlion head-in-sand generator.
- bgen/mimic via furniture.chest geometry plus teeth_row (detail.py:98) and stubby legs.
- A flying_serpent generator reusing bosses_pre2.eater_* segment logic with wings.
- Bone serpent head/segment reusing bosses_pre2.skeletron_skull (scaled) and a vertebra segment.
- An eater_of_souls worm-flyer and a crimera face-flyer (detail.organic).
- A fur-ball flinx.
- A shark variant of fauna.fish (dorsal fin, grey, teeth).
- An elemental rock or ice cluster.
Then point each enemy's `model` in data/enemies/*.json at the new entries.

findings.title: Non-human and themed enemies are recoloured humans; hat system has only cap/wide/hood/wreath
findings.evidence: 97 humanoid entries (assets.json). Only 3 set horns, 4 wings, 7 tail and 3 anatomy=skeleton. `hat` supports cap, wide, hood and wreath (accessories.py:32-60), and `cap` has a baseball visor (accessories.py:35-38). Yet hat=cap is given to santa_claus, party_girl, paladin, possessed_armor, hoplite, nutcracker, zombie_elf and skeleton_merchant. granite_golem, gingerbread_man, splinterling, mummy, eyezor, selenian, storm_diver, vortexian, yeti and ogre are plain humans with skin/shirt/pants colours only. For example mummy = `{skin #e8dcc0, shirt #e8dcc0, pants #e8dcc0}` with no bandages, and granite_golem = blue-skinned human in blue clothes. Tim (skeleton tinted #b08aff, no wizard hat), The Groom (zombie tinted #5a5a6a, no top hat), Undead Miner (no helmet/lamp), Angry Bones and Armored Skeleton all share `model: skeleton`/`zombie` with a tint (bestiary.json:55,58,59). Humanoid meshes are 28,851-71,213 tris, avg 54,138.
findings.terraria_reference: Tim's tall purple wizard hat, the Groom's top hat, the Undead Miner's lit mining helmet and Paladin's full plate are what identify these enemies. Mummies are bandaged, Eyezor has one giant eye, and Granite Golems are rock bodies. Santa and the Party Girl wear a Santa hat and a party cone.
findings.fix: Extend accessories.hat (accessories.py:28-60) with kinds 'wizard' (tall bent cone with star decals), 'top', 'santa' (cone plus pom-pom and fur rim), 'party' (striped cone), 'miner' (helmet plus a `char:glow` lamp) and 'helm' (full metal helmet with visor, `char:metal`). Add accessories.bandages (stripe mask painted on skin via paint.py), a giant eye (reuse head eyeball scaled), pointed ears for goblins, and a snout for werewolf and kobold. Give tim, the_groom, undead_miner, armored_skeleton and angry_bones their own assets.json creature entries with these params, and switch their `model` in data/enemies. For non-humanoid bodies (granite_golem, gingerbread_man, splinterling) write small detail.organic generators rigged with the shared human skeleton so they keep the human animation set.

findings.title: Event and late bosses are still primitive assemblies with no rig
findings.evidence: Tri counts: golem 928 (box blocks via _block, `return None`, so no rig; fists fused to the body), pumpking 916 (8 overlapping spheres plus box teeth), santa_nk1 248 (boxes), betsy 636 (spheres/tubes, no rig), mourning_wood 352, everscream 520, flying_dutchman 396, martian_saucer 588, martian_walker 344, the celestial pillars 912-1196, mothron 254, empress_of_light 2,544. manifest.json lists empty `animations` for 62 non-human creatures, including betsy, golem, pumpking, mourning_wood, everscream, santa_nk1, martian_walker and the four pillars. The master plan (line 55) already states that primitive-built bosses 'did not read as the reference game's'. The rebuilt bosses reach 7-18k tris (eye_of_cthulhu 10,558, deerclops 17,894).
findings.terraria_reference: Golem is a carved Lihzahrd idol whose head and two fists detach and fly. Pumpking is a jack-o'-lantern head with a cloak and scythe hands. Betsy is a large flapping dragon. Santa-NK1 is a detailed tank with a Santa hat and a face. The Mourning Wood is a gnarled screaming tree, and the pillars are ornate glowing columns.
findings.fix:
Port these to the boss-quality path used in bosses_pre/bosses_pre3: detail.organic metaball bodies with noise3 sculpt and painted vertex colour, plus teeth_row/spikes, and small rigs via creatures._action. Specifically:
- Golem: separate `golem_head` and `golem_fist` creature entries (renderer arms like the Skeletron hands, NpcRenderer.Arms.cs) with bevelled carved-stone blocks and glyph insets.
- Betsy: a rig with wing/neck/tail bones (copy the Duke Fishron DUKE_BONES pattern, bosses_lunar.py:86).
- Pumpking: an organic ribbed pumpkin, a cloak cloth, and hands with scythes as separate parts.
- Mourning Wood/Everscream: bark trunk via nature.py twisted-trunk code plus a carved face and a walk rig.
- Santa-NK1: bevelled hull, treads with wheels, Santa hat, face.
Budget 5-12k tris each. Move these generators out of festive.py/lunar.py into a new bosses_event.py to respect the 400-line cap.

findings.title: The most-seen enemies are the lowest-fidelity models, a big quality jump next to humans and bosses
findings.evidence:
- gel: 420 tris, 21 slime types share it (green/blue/black/yellow/mother/pinky/lava...). It uses opaque `prop:gel`, not `prop:gel:clear`, so the 'something swallowed' sphere at creatures.py:65 is hidden inside an opaque body. King Slime instead uses `_slime_body` with `prop:gel:clear` at 5,000 tris (bosses_pre.py:31).
- demon_eye: 550 tris (plain sphere plus 5 tube tentacles), shared by 5 enemies; the Eye of Cthulhu uses the detailed `_eyeball` (10,558 tris).
- cave_bat: 192 tris, 6 bat types.
- cursed_skull: 768 tris (old bosses.skull), vs skeletron_skull 7,794.
- wyvern: old Bore Tyrant `worm_segment` (bosses.py:69-90); wyvern_tail is 36 tris (one cone), wyvern_body 156.
- For comparison, humans average 54,138 tris.
findings.terraria_reference: Green and Blue Slimes are the first enemies players meet. They are translucent jelly with a visible item or gel core inside, and Demon Eyes have visible veins and a coloured iris. In Terraria these common sprites are drawn with the same care as boss sprites.
findings.fix:
Reuse the boss helpers at small budgets:
- gel: build the body with bosses_pre._slime_body(mb, 1.0, 0.8, '#ffffff', rng, alpha=0.7) at tris=1500 (the per-enemy `tint` already colours it) and bosses_pre._slime_face. Keep the inner sphere so drops show through the `:clear` shader.
- demon_eye: bosses_pre._eyeball(mb, 0.5, iris, rng, vein_trees=5, tris=1500, vein_depth=2) plus _optic_nerves(count=3).
- cursed_skull: bosses_pre2.skeletron_skull at radius 0.42 with a tris cap parameter.
- bat: detail.organic body with ears and a membrane wing polygon with finger struts.
- wyvern: a dedicated generator (dragon head with fur mane, segments with small legs, tail fin).
Move the shared helpers to detail.py if bosses_pre.py nears the 400-line cap. Target 1-3k tris for common enemies.

findings.title: Metal tier colours are muddy and collide (tint multiplied onto the grey iron texture)
findings.evidence: `METAL_LAYERS = {"copper": "copper", "gold": "gold"}` (build_all.py:29). Every other metal tints the `iron` layer (base #8a8e96), and both the shader (`albedo = a.rgb * COLOR.rgb * tint.rgb`) and the icon material multiply texture by colour. Measured icon medians: copper_broadsword #b9563b, palladium #9c6650, hellstone #93503d (three brown-oranges); crimtane #82424b vs adamantite #983b43; lead #555d6f; tungsten #697c6e. Bars: copper_bar #753627, gold_bar #9a6f28, hellstone_bar #5d3228, demonite_bar #383159, meteorite_bar #232223 (near black). The bar is two 12-tri extruded trapezoids (24 tris).
findings.terraria_reference:
Terraria's ore tiers are colour-coded and bright:
- copper: warm orange
- tin: pale khaki
- iron: grey
- lead: dark blue-grey
- silver: white
- tungsten: green
- gold: yellow
- platinum: pale blue-white
- demonite: purple-blue with sheen
- crimtane: red
- meteorite: rust-red
- hellstone: glowing orange-red with lava cracks
- cobalt: blue
- palladium: orange-salmon
- mythril: teal-green
- orichalcum: pink
- adamantite: red
- titanium: silver-blue
Bars are chunky ingots with a light top bevel.
findings.fix:
Add a neutral bright `silver` metal layer (base ~#d8dadf) in tools/textures/props.json and make it the default tint layer in build_all.plan (line 122). Then the assets.json `metals` colour is roughly what you see: the icon colour lands near the assets.json value instead of ~45% darker. Retune `metals` hexes against Terraria. Add per-metal accents via pattern params:
- hellstone and meteorite: `prop:plain:glow` crack veins (detail.veins on the bar/blade)
- demonite and crimtane: a darker edge colour
- hallowed: gold-white
Rebuild items.bar as a bevelled ingot (lathe or extrude with chamfer, a lighter top face colour, 3 stacked) at ~150 tris.

findings.title: Many items use an unrelated archetype, and some items are pixel-identical
findings.evidence:
- Herbs daybloom, moonglow, blinkroot, deathweed, waterleaf, fireblossom and shiverthorn use generator `feather` (a quill); so do turtle_shell, flipper, beetle_husk and hercules_beetle.
- wizard_hat, mining_helmet, jungle_hat and spectre_hood use the metal dome `helmet` (wizard_hat icon median #27282b, near black).
- death_sickle uses `axe`; lucy_the_axe is `axe` with no params (plain iron axe).
- The gold `ring` is used for compass, depth_meter, feral_claws, mana_flower, panic_necklace, cross_necklace, natures_gift and summoner_emblem (14 items).
- `chunk` (a 20-tri jittered icosphere) is used for obsidian_skull, cursed_flame, crystal_shard, cactus and all four lunar fragments.
- `spike` is used for unicorn_horn and shark_fin.
- `boots` (red cloth, 120 tris) is used for hermes, rocket, spectre, lightning and terraspark boots and tabi.
- `blob` (100 tris) is used for gel, flinx_fur, ectoplasm, truffle_worm and super_absorbant_sponge.
- Identical generator+params: lesser_healing_potion = healing_potion, lesser_mana_potion = mana_potion, wooden_arrow = flaming_arrow, bone = vertebra = bloody_spine, hook = grappling_hook, boomstick = shotgun, grenade = beenade, stardust_dragon_staff = spectre_staff, regeneration_potion = lifeforce_potion.
- All 29 potions share one 222-tri flask.
findings.terraria_reference: Terraria's herbs are flower sprites and the Wizard Hat is a tall blue star-spangled cone. The Mining Helmet has a lamp and the Death Sickle is a scythe. Lucy the Axe has a face on the blade. The Compass and Depth Meter are dials, and Hermes Boots have wings. Potion sizes are distinct (lesser = small round bottle, healing = flask, greater = tall). Flaming arrows burn, and the Obsidian Skull is a black skull.
findings.fix:
Add small generators in a new bgen/items_misc.py, registered in build_all.py:139:
- `herb`: reuse nature.flower petal geometry, unrooted.
- `soft_hat`: wizard cone with star decals, mining helmet with a glowing lamp, jungle hat.
- `scythe`: curved blade via extrude_polygon.
- `dial`: compass or depth meter, a disc plus a needle.
- `claw`, `skull_item`: reuse bosses.skull at small scale.
- `fragment`: a glowing crystal shard cluster in the pillar colours.
- `horn`: spiral lathe.
- `fin`: extruded fin.
- `boots` params: wings (hermes), a nozzle (rocket), lightning trim.
- potion `size`/`shape` params: lesser round, healing flask, greater tall.
- arrow `flame: true`: a glow tip.
Then re-point the listed assets.json entries.

findings.title: Equipped armour is never drawn on the player
findings.evidence: The only worn gear rendered is 'wings on the back ... flames under rocket boots and a puff of cloud' (PlayerAvatar.Gear.cs:8-11). A grep for armor/helmet in game/ finds only the inventory armour slots (InventoryScreen.cs:56-58). The helmet/chest_armor/greaves generators are icon props: a lathe dome plus a box (122 tris), a lathe barrel (156) and two cylinders (92). They can't be worn. The humanoid pipeline already fits garments to the 52-bone rig (garments.py, accessories.py).
findings.terraria_reference: In Terraria, each armour set visibly reskins the head, body and legs. It is one of the game's core progression rewards (Molten's flames, Hallowed gold, Shadow scales, Spectre hood). Vanity slots exist for the same reason.
findings.fix:
Generate wearable armour with bgen/human:
- Add a `human.build_armor(set_params)` that uses the Frame/body blob to fit shell garments: plate chest from the body mesh offset along normals, as the hood does in accessories.py:43-52, a helmet shell over the head, and greaves over the legs.
- Skin them with rig.write_weights to the shared armature.
- Export to assets/models/armor/<set>_{head,body,legs}.glb from a new `--armor` mode in build_all.py, with an `armor` table in assets.json (set -> style, metal tint, glow, extras like horns or visor).
- In game, add PlayerAvatar.Armor.cs: on armour-slot change, instance each piece's skinned mesh under the avatar's Skeleton3D (set the skin/skeleton path), and hide hair under helmets.
- Also route these meshes through SetLight (see the voxel-light finding).

findings.title: Fur, feathers and chitin all use the woven cloth texture; no bone/scale/fur layers exist
findings.evidence: The props atlas has 32 layers (256px, 8 columns): planks, dark_planks, stone, stone_brick, 5 barks, leaves/fronds/sprigs, cactus_skin, glowcap, red_cap, iron, dark_iron, gold, copper, cloth, red_cloth, leather, clay, crystal, flesh, gel, plain, missing. There is no fur, feather, scale, chitin or bone layer. Bat fur (`prop:cloth`, creatures.py:98), vulture feathers (fauna.py:30), hornet body (fauna.py:159-164), steed mane (beasts.py:112) and all feathered wings (`layer = ... 'prop:cloth'`, gear.py:35) use woven cloth. The angel_wings icon median is #858178, a grey knit, where assets.json says #f8f4ec. Crab and antlion shells use `prop:clay`, and skulls/bones use `prop:plain`.
findings.terraria_reference: Terraria's creatures read by material: glossy chitin on hornets and beetles, soft white feathers on Angel Wings and Harpies, fur on bunnies and wolves, bone on skeletons.
findings.fix: Add props.json layers `fur` (directional strands, type 'grass'-like generator in gen_plants.py or gen_natural.py), `feather` (barbs with a light shaft), `scales` (overlapping scallops), `chitin` (glossy, roughness 0.25) and `bone` (porous ivory). Rebuild with tools/textures/build_textures.py --set=props. Switch the slots in gear.wings (feather style uses `prop:feather`), creatures.bat, fauna.bird/insect/crab, beasts.steed and critters.* to the new layers. Keep cloth for actual cloth.

findings.title: Third-person held item and worn wings ignore voxel light (sky-lit in caves)
findings.evidence: CreatureVisual.SetLight writes `voxel_light` only to `_geometry`, which Setup collects from the GLB scene (CreatureVisual.cs:65-72, 131). The held MeshInstance3D is attached later via AttachToBone (PlayerAvatar.cs:94,111), and the wings are added as a child of the avatar (Gear.cs:90). Neither is in `_geometry`, and nothing else sets their light (grep: only ViewModel.cs:77 does, for first person). They keep the shader default `instance uniform vec4 voxel_light = vec4(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)`: sky exposure 1, so AO = 1 and `strata_sun_gate` = smoothstep(0.35,0.95,1) = 1, with no torch block light.
findings.terraria_reference: Terraria lights held items and worn accessories with the same tile light as the player sprite, so a sword in a dark cave is dark and a torch-lit one is warm.
findings.fix: In PlayerAvatar._Process, after `_visual.SetLight(light)` (line 52), also call SetInstanceShaderParameter("voxel_light", light) on `_held` (if it is a GeometryInstance3D) and `_wings`. Alternatively, have CreatureVisual.AttachToBone register GeometryInstance3D descendants into `_geometry` so SetLight/SetTint cover attachments automatically; this also covers future armour pieces.

findings.title: Furniture and crafting stations are unbevelled box assemblies
findings.evidence: Object GLB tris: wooden_chest 70, gold_chest 70, wooden_table 72, iron_anvil 76, torch 80, furnace 112, wooden_door 124, bed 128, work_bench 136, wooden_chair 96, tombstone 92, pressure_plate 24. furniture.py is almost entirely `mb.box` calls (e.g. table 21-23, chair 99-107, bed 155-161, chest 128-133), and MeshBuilder.box has no bevel (mesh.py:80-87). Trees are 2,086-2,850 tris with leaf cards, so furniture looks cruder than the world around it. The inventory icons for placeables render these meshes (41 items use `object` icons).
findings.terraria_reference: Terraria's Wooden Chest (banded, gold latch), Iron Anvil (a horned anvil silhouette), Furnace (stone with a glowing mouth) and Work Bench are recognisable at a glance and appear constantly in player bases.
findings.fix: Add `bevel` (and optional `seams`) options to MeshBuilder.box using bmesh.ops.bevel on the new part's edges (width 0.01-0.02, 2 segments) and call it from furniture generators. Add plank seams on tables and chests (thin inset boxes or vertex-colour darkening), metal corner brackets on chests, an arched lid, a proper horned anvil profile with a waisted base (lathe), and a glowing mouth plus coals on the furnace. Budget 400-1,500 tris per object.

findings.title: Dropped items are flat Y-billboards with a hard alpha cut and a faint rarity glow
findings.evidence: Drops are a 1 m QuadMesh scaled to 0.38 m (0.3 m for blocks) with a Y-axis billboard. `if (tex.a < 0.5) discard;` gives a hard edge on a 128px Cycles icon with no outline. Glow is `item.Stack.Item.Rarity > 0 ? 0.08f : 0f`. A 3D model exists for 660 items (manifest) but drops don't use it.
findings.terraria_reference: Terraria drops show the item sprite at native size, with a rarity-coloured glint/sparkle for rare items and a pulsing shine, which makes loot pickup feel rewarding.
findings.fix: For non-block items, draw the GLB model (PropLibrary.Model) slowly spinning and bobbing, lit with voxel_light. Fall back to the sprite for placeables. Add a rarity-coloured additive rim or particle glint (CpuParticles3D like PlayerAvatar.Gear.cs:50-66) keyed off Rarity. If sprites stay, use alpha-to-coverage (`alpha_antialiasing_mode`) and the outlined icons from the icon finding.

findings.title: Baseline that works: the rebuilt pre-hardmode and hardmode bosses read as their Terraria counterparts
findings.evidence: King Slime 7,030 tris (translucent :clear gel, crown, trapped ninja, bosses_pre.py:85-91). Eye of Cthulhu 10,558 (veined eyeball, cornea, optic nerves) and its maw 11,428. Brain of Cthulhu 10,320 / 13,830. Twins ~9,276. Skeletron 7,794. Wall of Flesh eye 10,610 and mouth 5,602. Deerclops 17,894 (rigged). All are built with detail.organic metaballs, noise sculpt, painted vertex colour, veins, teeth_ring and fang.
findings.terraria_reference: These match Terraria's silhouettes and colour identities (blue slime with a crown, veined eye with a blue iris, a pink brain, a skull with hands).
findings.fix: Use these helpers (detail.organic, bosses_pre._eyeball/_slime_body/_crown, bosses_pre2.skeletron_skull) as the house style for every other creature and item upgrade above. Move the reusable helpers from bosses_pre.py into detail.py so fauna/creatures modules can import them without cross-boss dependencies. Delete or retire the superseded generators still registered in bosses.py:221-225 (gel_sovereign, watcher, worm_segment, skull), mechs.py:189 and horrors.py:142 once the wyvern and cursed_skull stop using them.

summary: I checked the four digests against the code and found 21 more things a Terraria player would notice straight away. None of them is in the digests. The biggest one is that opening the inventory freezes the character. Movement, jumping, hotbar keys and item use all stop, yet the world keeps running because auto-pause is off by default. So a player sorting items can be killed while unable to move. Right-click in the inventory follows Minecraft rules (take half / place one). It cannot equip armor or open crates, and there is no hold-to-take-one. Several core Terraria loops are simply absent: enemies never drop hearts or mana stars, Fallen Stars never fall at night (even though their own description says they do), and swords and projectiles cannot smash pots or cut grass. Loot has quieter gaps. Prefixes are only rolled on crafted items, never on drops, chest loot or shop buys. 19 of 20 buff potions have tooltips that don't say what they do or for how long. Debuffs have no visuals, and there is no invasion progress bar. Smaller polish bugs round this out: raw station ids like "hardmode_anvil" in the crafting UI, the item magnet pulling items into the player when the inventory is full, and ItemDef.SoundSet being defined but never used.

findings.title: Opening the inventory freezes the player (no moving, jumping, hotbar keys or item use) while the world keeps running
findings.evidence: InputGate: "While any is open, gameplay input (movement, camera look, item use) is ignored." PlayerController: `var input = blocked ? Vector2.Zero : Input.GetVector(...)`; jump is also gated on `!blocked`. InteractionController._UnhandledInput returns when GameplayBlocked, so the 1-0 keys and the mouse wheel stop working. InventoryScreen only pauses when `AutoPause`, and AutoPause defaults to false, so enemies keep attacking a player who cannot move.
findings.terraria_reference: The inventory is an overlay. You keep full control: walk, jump, fight, switch hotbar slots with number keys and the wheel, and even use the held item by clicking the world. Players constantly sort items mid-fight or while running.
findings.fix: Split InputGate layers into kinds: `BlocksAll` (pause, console, text entry) and `FreesMouse` (inventory, chest, town dialog). PlayerController and the jump/grapple/dash code should read keyboard movement unless a BlocksAll layer is open. InteractionController should keep handling hotbar_1..10 and the wheel while only FreesMouse layers are open. Wheel input should be ignored when the mouse is over a panel (GetViewport().GuiGetHoveredControl()). Optionally let a held right mouse button rotate the camera while the inventory is open. Leave AutoPause as opt-in.

findings.title: Inventory right-click uses Minecraft rules: takes half or places one; no equip-swap, no opening crates, no hold-to-take-more
findings.evidence: SlotActions.RightClick: `int half = (s.Count + 1) / 2; cursor = s.WithCount(half);`, and with a cursor stack it places one: `inv[slot] = cursor.WithCount(1)`. ItemSlotView fires only once per press. Armor and accessories equip only through shift-click with no chest open (PlayerInventory.Equip). Crates open only by holding them in the hotbar and using them (ItemUseSystem.Open).
findings.terraria_reference: Right-click on a stack picks up ONE item onto the cursor, and holding the button speeds up. Right-click on armor or an accessory equips it, swapping with what is worn. Right-click on crates, bags and presents opens them in place. Right-click never splits a stack in half or drops one.
findings.fix: Rewrite SlotActions.RightClick. With the cursor empty or holding the same item, move 1 from the slot to the cursor. If the slot item has an EquipSlot, call PlayerInventory.Equip (make it swap for accessories). If ItemUseTable shows the item opens a loot table, call a new ItemUseSystem.OpenFromSlot(player, slot). In ItemSlotView, track how long the right button is held and repeat Clicked at a rate that speeds up (every 0.5 s at first, down to 1 frame). Update the SlotActions tests.

findings.title: Enemies never drop heart or mana-star pickups
findings.evidence: NpcSystem.Kill drops only loot-table rolls and coins. No heart or mana_star item exists (grep 'heart'/'star_pickup' finds nothing in data or src). The item behavior list (meleeSwing … paint) has no on-pickup heal.
findings.terraria_reference: Killing an enemy while you are hurt has a good chance to drop a pulsing Heart that heals 20 life on touch. Mana Stars drop when your mana is low and restore mana. Bosses spill several hearts. This is a core part of the fight-and-sustain loop.
findings.fix: Add `heart` and `mana_star` items with a new `pickupEffect` behavior ({healLife:20} / {healMana:100}, never stored). In NpcSystem.Kill, roll them based on the nearest player's missing life or mana (more rolls for bosses). In the GameWorld drop-collector callback, apply the heal instead of calling Inventory.Pickup, then raise an event so CombatEffects shows the green or blue number. Render them as bobbing, glowing sprites with a point light.

findings.title: Swords and projectiles cannot break pots or cut grass and vines
findings.evidence: HitObject is only called from the tool path (`else if (info.IsTool && inReach != null)`). For BreakTool.Any it needs `Math.Max(PickPower, AxePower, HammerPower) > 0`, so a sword gets WrongTool. MeleeSystem only sweeps NPCs, and ProjectileSystem never touches TileObjects. Pots (`hitPoints: 1`, no breakTool) can therefore only be broken with a pickaxe, axe or hammer.
findings.terraria_reference: Pots shatter from any melee swing, projectile or thrown item, and smashing them while exploring caves is a constant small reward. Sword swings also cut tall grass, vines and flowers, sometimes dropping seeds.
findings.fix: Add a TileObjectDef flag `breakByAttack` (set it for pots, grass and plant decor). In MeleeSystem.Tick, test the swing arc against TileObjects.InBox and call editor.BreakObject. In ProjectileSystem collision, break flagged objects the projectile touches. Play a pot-shatter sound and shard dust through the existing ObjectBroken event.

findings.title: Fallen Stars never fall at night, even though their description says they do
findings.evidence: The fallen_star description reads "Falls from the night sky", but nothing in src/ spawns it: a grep for fallen_star/FallingStar in src is empty, and the 'world' tag only exempts it from the validator's source check. Its only sources are cave_bat (2%), jellyfish/hellbat (3%) and one container, yet a Mana Crystal costs 5.
findings.terraria_reference: Every night, stars streak down with a whoosh and a glowing trail, land, glow on the ground and vanish at dawn. Collecting them is the classic early-night activity and the main route to Mana Crystals.
findings.fix: Add a StarfallDirector (Strata.Core/Gameplay/Events, ticked by GameWorld at night). It spawns a `falling_star` projectile high above players at a data-driven rate per chunk column. On hitting terrain it turns into a dropped fallen_star with light, and uncollected stars despawn at dawn. The renderer gets a bright trail, a point light and a star_fall sound. Tune the rate in data/events.json or data/config.

findings.title: Prefixes are rolled only on crafted items, never on drops, chest loot or shop purchases
findings.evidence: Prefixes.Fresh is called only in RecipeBook.Craft and the angler reward. LootRoller builds `new ItemStack(item, n)` and TownCommerce.Buy builds `new ItemStack(item, count)`, both without a prefix. Every chest Hermes Boots, Enchanted Sword, boss drop and bought Copper Pickaxe is therefore unprefixed.
findings.terraria_reference: Any weapon, tool or accessory gets a random prefix (Legendary, Warding, Menacing…) whether it is crafted, dropped by an enemy or boss, found in a chest or bought from a shop. Checking the prefix on new loot is part of the thrill.
findings.fix: Add a helper Prefixes.Roll(ItemStack, content, ref rng) that applies Fresh when Count == 1 and the item can take a prefix. Call it in LootRoller for every produced stack (this covers enemy, boss, crate and chest loot via EnsureContainerLoot) and in TownCommerce.Buy. Add a test.

findings.title: Potion and buff tooltips don't say what the item does or how long it lasts
findings.evidence: ItemTooltip.Lines never reads `item.Buff`. 19 of the 20 buff-granting items have no description (regeneration, shine, night_owl, spelunker, mining, builder, archery, endurance, ironskin …). 10 of the 39 buff definitions (on_fire, poisoned, ironskin, regeneration, swiftness …) also have no description. So hovering Ironskin Potion shows only the name, 'Consumable' and the sell price. The damage and crit lines also use the item's base values (`item.Damage`, `4 + item.Crit`) and ignore the player's bonuses.
findings.terraria_reference: The tooltip reads 'Ironskin Potion / Increases defense by 8 / 5 minute duration / Consumable'. Weapon damage and crit lines show your effective values with your current class bonuses, and items with no value say 'No value'.
findings.fix: In ItemTooltip.Lines, when item.Buff is set, add the buff's description (or text generated from its stat effects, e.g. '+8 defense', '25% increased movement speed') and a duration line ('5 minute duration'). Fill in the missing buff descriptions in data. Pass the player's stats into Lines so the damage and crit lines go through DamageModel, and add 'No value' when Value == 0.

findings.title: Buffs and debuffs have no visuals on the player or enemies
findings.evidence: NPC tint is `Color.FromHtml(npc.Def.Tint)` or the hurt flash, and nothing else. A grep for debuff/OnFire/Poisoned in game/ finds only the HUD buff row. Flames are used only for torches and rocket boots. The only visible buff effect is on_fire's `emitLight`.
findings.terraria_reference: On Fire! gives off flames and embers, Poisoned tints green and drips, Ichor drips yellow, Frostburn shows blue flames, Chilled and Slow tint blue. The same effects appear on the player, so you can see at a glance that a flask or debuff is working.
findings.fix: Add an optional `visual` block to BuffDef (tint, dustColor, dustRate, flame). Add a StatusVisuals node that iterates NPC and player buffs, blends the tint into SetTint, and attaches a pooled GPUParticles3D (reusing Flames for fire types) to each afflicted body.

findings.title: The item magnet pulls items in even when the inventory is full, so they hover inside the player
findings.evidence: `if (it.PickupDelay == 0 && dist < MagnetRange)` attracts every item regardless of space. Inside PickupRange, when tryCollect returns a remainder, the item keeps its velocity with no gravity, so it overshoots, gets pulled back and orbits the player. MagnetRange is a const with no grab-range stat.
findings.terraria_reference: Items only fly to you when they fit (Player.ItemSpace); otherwise they stay on the ground. Treasure Magnet and Celestial Magnet extend the grab range.
findings.fix: Pass a `canTake` predicate to DroppedItemSystem.Tick (Backpack.CanFit or a partial-fit check) and magnetize only when it is true. Otherwise apply normal gravity and friction. Replace the MagnetRange constant with a per-player value built from StatIds.GrabRange and add magnet accessories.

findings.title: An item on the cursor cannot be thrown by clicking outside the inventory
findings.evidence: The inventory root uses MouseFilter.Ignore and nothing handles clicks on empty space. The cursor stack is only stowed back into the backpack when the screen closes (SlotActions.Stow). A grep for Inventory.Cursor shows no other use.
findings.terraria_reference: Left-clicking the world with an item on the cursor throws the whole stack; right-click throws one. This is how players dump junk quickly.
findings.fix: Add a full-screen transparent Control under the panels with MouseFilter.Stop. On left click with a non-empty cursor, call Drops.Spawn(cursor, Eye + Aim*0.6, Aim*5 + up, pickupDelay: 90) and clear the cursor; right click throws one. Play a throw sound.

findings.title: No invasion or event progress bar
findings.evidence: Nine events have a killGoal (e.g. pumpkin_moon 250, frost_moon 250, frost_legion 80, old_ones_army 140) and EventDirector tracks `a.Kills`, but game/ reads KillGoal only in SoundEvents to pick a start sound. The HUD has a boss bar and nothing for events.
findings.terraria_reference: During invasions a panel in the bottom-right shows the event icon, its name and a progress bar with a percentage. Pumpkin and Frost Moon show 'Wave N: <enemy>'.
findings.fix: Add an EventProgress panel to the HUD, bound to the active events with KillGoal > 0: name, a bar of Kills/KillGoal, and the wave label when the event defines waves. Hide it when no such event is running and fade it out on completion.

findings.title: The crafting UI shows raw station ids ('hardmode_anvil', 'tinkerers_workshop', 'alchemy')
findings.evidence: `"Near: " + string.Join(", ", env.Stations...)` and `"At: " + string.Join(", ", r.Def.Stations)` print ids straight from the data. The data uses ids like ancient_manipulator (39 recipes), hardmode_anvil (26), alchemy (22) and work_bench (12). The Guide's help prints the same ids ('(at hardmode_anvil)').
findings.terraria_reference: Recipes list 'Required objects: Mythril Anvil' and 'Placed Bottle' with proper names, and alternatives are named explicitly.
findings.fix: Add a station display-name map, derived from the TileObjectDef names that provide each station plus aliases for groups (hardmode_anvil → 'Mythril or Orichalcum Anvil', alchemy → 'Placed Bottle or Alchemy Table', hardmode_forge → 'Adamantite or Titanium Forge'). Use it in CraftingPanel and TownDialog.

findings.title: Guide help and Goblin reforge work on the held item and reply in text; the shop has no buyback
findings.evidence: CraftHelp: "Hold an item and ask again", then prints a comma-separated list of what it makes. Reforge acts on `_ui.Inventory.Held` and reports 'Reforged: {made}' with the coin sound, with no before/after stats. ShowShop has buy rows plus 'Sell held stack', and a grep for buyback finds nothing.
findings.terraria_reference: The Guide has an item slot; dropping an item in shows a grid of every recipe it is used in, with materials and stations. The Goblin Tinkerer has a reforge slot showing the cost; you click the hammer repeatedly, hear the anvil sound and watch the prefix change in the tooltip. Shops keep a buyback list of recently sold items.
findings.fix: In TownDialog, add an ItemSlotView bound to a one-slot Inventory for the Guide and Goblin services, sharing the cursor with InventoryScreen and opening the inventory alongside. Render the Guide's results with CraftingPanel's rows. Keep the Reforge button active for repeated clicks with a 'reforge' sound and a live tooltip. Add a buyback queue in TownCommerce, filled from Sell and shown as a final shop row.

findings.title: No Piggy Bank, Safe or other portable storage
findings.evidence: A grep for 'piggy' across data/src/game finds nothing. The Merchant sells torch, bottle, arrows, potions, copper tools, bucket, rope, bug net and mining helmet only. Only wooden and gold chests are containers.
findings.terraria_reference: The Piggy Bank (1 gold, from the Merchant) is one of the first purchases: shared personal storage reachable from any base. The Safe, Defender's Forge and Void Vault follow later, along with the Money Trough and Void Bag for portable access.
findings.fix: Add piggy_bank and safe tile objects with interaction 'chest' and a `sharedStorage` key. Store the contents on PlayerState (saved with the character) instead of on the object. Add them to the Merchant shop, with the Safe after the Skeletron flag.

findings.title: Per-item use sounds are unused: ItemDef.SoundSet is never read, so whole weapon families share one sound
findings.evidence: `public string? SoundSet { get; init; }` has no readers and no data sets `soundSet`. OnUsed plays 'swing' for every melee item. ShotSound picks between bow, gun or gun_heavy, and magic or magic_heavy, then falls back to 'swing' for boomerangs, shuriken and yoyos. All food and misc consumables play 'heal'.
findings.terraria_reference: Every item has its own UseSound: Item1 swing, Item5 bow, Item11 pistol, Item36 shotgun, Item40 sniper, Item8/Item20/Item43 staffs, Item2 eating, Item3 drinking, Item4 Life Crystal, Item29 Mana Crystal, and so on. Weapons are recognised by ear.
findings.fix: In SoundEvents.OnUsed, play item.SoundSet first when Sfx.Has() it, and otherwise fall back to the current family rules. Add soundSet values in the item JSON for families (shotgun, sniper, staff types, thrown, eat, crystal) and add the matching sound files.

findings.title: Speed accessories feel flat: Hermes Boots is an instant +45% and a Sprint key speeds everyone up
findings.evidence: The boots' description says "Sprint far faster once you get going", but the only effect is `{stat: moveSpeed, add: 0.45}`, applied to walk speed from a standstill (groundAcceleration 40 reaches it in about 0.2 s). Shift sprint multiplies by 1.35 for every character. There is no run dust or boot-specific sound.
findings.terraria_reference: There is no sprint key. Hermes-type boots raise top speed only after a run-up, kicking up a dust or cloud trail, and the run-up to boot speed is a signature Terraria feel.
findings.fix: Add a 'runBoost' equip effect (accelTime, maxSpeedBonus, dustColor). PlayerController ramps the extra top speed after about 0.4 s of continuous ground running and spawns trail particles. Consider making the Shift sprint smaller, or the thing these boots unlock, so movement upgrades stay meaningful.

findings.title: Chest lids never open
findings.evidence: ObjectPlacement changes the transform only for levers (`Switch && o.Active`) and doors (`Door && o.Active`). The chest lid is extruded into the same single mesh as the body, and nothing reacts to ContainerOpened except the chest_open sound.
findings.terraria_reference: A chest shows its open frame (lid up) while its contents are on screen, and closes with a sound when you walk away.
findings.fix: Export the chest lid as a separate named node in the Blender generator. In TileObjectRenderer, hinge the lid open while InventoryScreen has that chest open (hook ContainerOpened and CloseContainer) with a short tween, and add a chest_close sound.

findings.title: No pets or light pets, and no vanity or dye items in the data
findings.evidence: The Pet, Vanity and Dye categories exist, but a grep for items using those categories returns 0, and nothing in src/game references them. The Shadow Orb loot table rolls Musket, Vilethorn, Ball O' Hurt and Band of Starpower, but not the Shadow Orb light pet.
findings.terraria_reference: From the early game players collect pets and light pets (Shadow Orb, Crimson Heart, Fairy Bell, Magic Lantern, Wisp) that follow them and light caves. This is a big part of Terraria's charm and personalisation, alongside vanity and dye.
findings.fix: Add pet and light-pet equipment slots (misc equipment) and a PetSystem that spawns a follower using the existing minion movement and renderer. Light pets emit light through DynamicLights. Add the orb/heart light pets to the evil loot tables, and add a first batch of vanity and dye items once the vanity slots exist.

findings.title: No achievements or achievement popups
findings.evidence: A grep for 'achievement' across src, game and data finds nothing. Progression milestones exist (ItemDef.Milestone, Progression.Raised) but show only as banner announcements.
findings.terraria_reference: Achievement toasts with an icon ('Timber!!', 'Benched', 'Ooo! Shiny!', 'Heart Breaker', 'Hold on Tight!') appear in the corner, lead new players through the early game and give a steady stream of small rewards.
findings.fix: Add a data-driven Achievements system in Strata.Core/Gameplay/Progression, triggered from existing events (ItemPickedUp, Craft, BossDefeated, ObjectPlaced, Milestone), saved per player. Show a HUD corner toast with an icon plus a list page in the pause menu.

findings.title: No Treasure Bags: Expert-only loot drops loose
findings.evidence: The eye_of_cthulhu loot table drops lens, demonite and mana_crystal directly, with `shield_of_cthulhu` behind `{type: difficulty, min: 1}`. No item with 'bag' in its id exists, and boss loot bursts out as loose drops.
findings.terraria_reference: In Expert and Master, each boss drops a rarity-coloured Treasure Bag that you right-click to open. It holds the loot plus an Expert-only item, and opening it is a signature item moment.
findings.fix: Add a `<boss>_treasure_bag` item per boss (category Container, Rarity -12, opens the boss's loot table plus the expert item). In NpcSystem.Kill, drop the bag instead of loose loot when the world difficulty is Expert or higher. This depends on right-click opening from the inventory.

findings.title: Controls ignore Terraria habits, and the wheel hotbar actions are dead
findings.evidence: `hotbar_next`/`hotbar_prev` are defined and listed for rebinding, but the code hard-codes `MouseButton.WheelDown/WheelUp`, so rebinding them does nothing. Q drops one item (Ctrl+Q drops the stack). Esc opens the pause menu, not the inventory.
findings.terraria_reference: Terraria defaults: Esc opens the inventory, T throws the whole stack, H/J/B quick heal/mana/buff, E grapple, Ctrl toggles smart cursor, Shift auto-select. Veterans reach for these keys straight away.
findings.fix: Read the hotbar_next/hotbar_prev actions instead of the hard-coded wheel. Make drop_item throw the whole stack by default (Terraria T) with a modifier for one. Offer a 'Terraria layout' preset in SettingsScreen.Controls that rebinds to the reference keys, keeping the 3D build keys (shape/rotate) on free keys.
